title: Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound in the Diagnosis of Parotid Gland Castleman Disease in a Child.
abstract: Castleman disease is a rare lymphoproliferative disorder that infrequently involves the parotid gland. We report a 16-year-old girl with a 3-year history of slowly progressive, painless right cheek swelling. CT and MRI showed an avidly enhancing, markedly T2-hyperintense parotid lesion, suggesting a vascular malformation; fine-needle aspiration yielded reactive lymphoid tissue. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) demonstrated rapid, intense, homogeneous enhancement, confirming a hypervascular solid mass rather than a vascular malformation and raising suspicion for Castleman disease. Superficial parotidectomy confirmed unicentric hyaline-vascular Castleman disease. CEUS aided differentiation of a hypervascular solid lesion from a vascular malformation and narrowed the differential.

title: An Echocardiogram-Based Ultrasound Radiomic Model Predicts Recovery of Coronary Artery Diameter in Kawasaki Disease.
abstract: Objective To develop a predictive model based on echocardiogram-based ultrasound radiomic features for the recovery of coronary artery diameter in Kawasaki disease (KD) with coronary artery lesions (CALs). Methods A total of 206 children with acute KD and left CALs who underwent coronary ultrasound before and 8 weeks after treatment were retrospectively enrolled. The patients were randomly divided into training and testing sets at a 7:3 ratio. Ultrasound radiomic features were extracted from regions of interest delineated along the coronary artery wall on pretreatment ultrasound images. Machine learning models based on five different algorithms, including logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), random forest, extra trees, and light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), were established to predict the recovery of coronary artery diameter. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic efficiency of the models, and the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were calculated. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was used to evaluate the clinical benefits of the use of the models. Results Based on Z score normalization of coronary artery diameters, diameters returned to normal in 77 patients in the training set and 37 in the testing set, whereas 67 and 25 patients, respectively, showed no such recovery after treatment. A total of 1562 ultrasound radiomic features were extracted; following the use of feature selection processes, 9 optimally performing features were employed for machine learning model development. The LightGBM model showed the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC, sensitivity, and specificity of 0.867 (95% CI: 0.811-0.923), 59.7%, and 97.0%, respectively, in the training set and of 0.857 (95% CI: 0.756-0.958), 86.5%, and 76.0%, respectively, in the testing set. DCA revealed that over a threshold range of 0.4 ~ 0.8, the model offers good clinical benefits. Conclusion Machine learning models can predict the recovery of coronary artery diameter in KD and thus may offer important value for clinical decision-making.

title: Multimodal Ultrasound for Early Prognostic Assessment During Definitive Radiotherapy in Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the prognostic value of early multimodal ultrasound parameters in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included 31 patients with histologically confirmed cervical squamous cell carcinoma who underwent definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy. Grayscale ultrasound and shear wave elastography (SWE) were performed in all patients at baseline and approximately 2 weeks after radiotherapy initiation, whereas complete contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) data were available for 22 patients. Unfavorable outcomes were defined as progression, recurrence, or death during follow-up after radiotherapy initiation. ROC analysis was performed to evaluate individual parameters, and a logistic regression model incorporating baseline SWE mean and tumor maximum diameter at the two-week assessment was internally validated using 1000 bootstrap resamples to estimate optimism-corrected performance. Exploratory time-dependent ROC analyses were performed using progression-free survival data to assess model discrimination at different follow-up time points. Results Patients with unfavorable outcomes showed higher baseline SWE mean values (153 vs. 106.5 kPa, p = 0.039) and larger residual tumor maximum diameters 2 weeks after radiotherapy initiation (36 vs. 32 mm, p = 0.045). The combined model showed an apparent AUC of 0.775 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.735. Exploratory time-dependent ROC analysis yielded AUC values of 0.855, 0.840, and 0.719 at 12, 24, and 36 months, respectively. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated shorter progression-free survival in the higher-risk group than in the lower-risk group according to the combined model (log-rank p = 0.022). In exploratory CEUS subgroup analysis, a greater reduction in time to peak was associated with unfavorable outcomes (p = 0.039). Conclusions Baseline tumor stiffness and early residual tumor size assessed by multimodal ultrasound may offer complementary prognostic information for exploratory risk stratification in patients with LACC undergoing definitive radiotherapy. Further prospective validation is warranted.

title: Sonographic Diagnosis and Anatomic Mapping of a Radial Artery Pseudoaneurysm Following Transradial Cardiac Catheterization.
abstract: Radial artery pseudoaneurysm is a rare complication of transradial catheterization. We report a 74-year-old woman on rivaroxaban who developed a pulsatile distal forearm mass 1 day after transradial cardiac catheterization. High-frequency ultrasound showed a rounded extra-arterial lesion (7.6 × 8.9 × 7.0 mm) not involving all wall layers, with thrombus, a discrete communicating neck, turbulent bidirectional "yin-yang" color Doppler, and preserved distal flow. Anatomic mapping showed the lesion abutting adjacent tendons and the palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve. Surgical excision and microscopic repair succeeded. Sonographic characterization provided anatomic detail that, with clinical and surgical assessment, informed individualized management.

title: Surgical approach and insert constraint are associated with small differences in patellar tilt after robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty: A retrospective comparative radiographic study.
abstract: Purpose Patellofemoral alignment remains important after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Robotic-assisted functional positioning may reduce the impact of approach- and implant-related factors on the patellofemoral joint. This study evaluated the association between surgical approach and insert constraint with postoperative static patellar alignment following robotic-assisted TKA. Methods This retrospective comparative radiographic study included 320 primary nonresurfaced robotic-assisted TKA performed with the MAKO system between March 2021 and December 2024. Patients were divided into four groups: mini-subvastus condylar-stabilised (MSV-CS, n = 134), mini-subvastus posterior-stabilised (MSV-PS, n = 63), medial parapatellar condylar-stabilised (MPP-CS, n = 75) and medial parapatellar posterior-stabilised (MPP-PS, n = 48). Standardised Merchant axial radiographs at 30° and lateral radiographs were obtained at 2 months and 1 year. Patellar tilt was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes were qualitative patellar centreing, patellar thickness and the modified Blackburne-Peel index. Two-way factorial analysis assessed surgical approach, insert constraint and their interaction. Results Baseline characteristics and final intraoperative robotic alignment parameters were comparable across groups. MSV and CS implants were associated with statistically greater patellar tilt than MPP and PS implants, respectively, but the absolute differences were small, approximately 1°. No significant interaction was observed between surgical approach and insert constraint. Patellar height did not differ between groups. Conclusion Robotic-assisted functional positioning provided consistent static patellofemoral alignment regardless of surgical approach or insert constraint. Although statistically significant differences in patellar tilt were detected, their approximately 1° magnitude suggests a negligible radiographic effect. Their clinical significance remains unknown because clinical outcomes and dynamic patellar tracking were not assessed. Level of evidence Level IV.

Two-way factorial analysis assessed surgical approach, insert constraint and their interaction.

Results

Baseline characteristics and final intraoperative robotic alignment parameters were comparable across groups. MSV and CS implants were associated with statistically greater patellar tilt than MPP and PS implants, respectively, but the absolute differences were small, approximately 1°. No significant interaction was observed between surgical approach and insert constraint. Patellar height did not differ between groups.

Conclusion

Robotic-assisted functional positioning provided consistent static patellofemoral alignment regardless of surgical approach or insert constraint. Although statistically significant differences in patellar tilt were detected, their approximately 1° magnitude suggests a negligible radiographic effect. Their clinical significance remains unknown because clinical outcomes and dynamic patellar tracking were not assessed.

Level of evidence

Level IV.

title: Single-strand superficial medial collateral ligament reconstruction with a peroneus longus split graft provides reliable control of anteromedial rotatory instability combined with anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A 2-year clinical cohort study.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate 2-year clinical, radiological, and patient-reported outcomes after combined anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction and single-strand superficial medial collateral ligament (sMCL) reconstruction using a peroneus longus split graft (PLSG) in patients with anteromedial rotatory instability (AMRI). Methods Patients with ACL insufficiency and clinically and intraoperatively confirmed AMRI who underwent combined ACL and sMCL reconstruction using a PLSG were retrospectively identified and prospectively followed. AMRI was diagnosed in this study based on a combination of ACL insufficiency, increased anteromedial drawer in external tibial rotation, medial laxity on valgus stress testing at 20° of knee flexion, pivot-shift grading as an indicator of overall rotatory instability of the knee, and supportive arthroscopic findings such as the medial meniscus squeeze sign. At a minimum follow-up of 2 years, 59 of 63 patients (mean age 30 years, 48% female) were available for evaluation. Postoperative stability was assessed using KT-1000 instrumented side-to-side measurements for the Lachman test and anterior drawer test at 90° flexion with neutral and 15° external tibial rotation (AMRI-related). Pivot-shift grading and valgus stress radiographs obtained at 20° of knee flexion were additionally performed. Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) included International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) Subjective, Lysholm, Tegner activity scale, and return-to-any-sport rate. A non-inferiority margin of 3 mm for side-to-side differences was predefined. Results The mean side-to-side difference for the AMRI-related anterior drawer was 0.0 ± 1.3 mm (95% CI: -0.4 to 0.3 mm), meeting the predefined non-inferiority criterion (upper one-sided 95% confidence limit 0.3 mm; p < 0.001). The mean Lachman side-to-side difference was 1.8 mm ± 1.3 mm and remained within clinically acceptable limits. A negative pivot-shift was observed in 93% of patients. IKDC (59 ± 20 to 85 ± 12; p < 0.001) and Lysholm (61 ± 25 to 89 ± 11; p < 0.001) scores improved significantly, whereas the Tegner Activity Scale (5.8 ± 1.7 to 5.2 ± 1.6; p = 0.007) showed a small but significant decrease. The mean side-to-side difference in medial joint opening on valgus stress radiographs was 0.6 mm ± 1.0 mm, remaining below the predefined clinical reference threshold. At 2 years, 66% of patients had returned to any sports. Conclusion Combined ACL and single-strand sMCL reconstruction using a PLSG was associated with low postoperative side-to-side differences, satisfactory postoperative stability, favourable postoperative PROMs and low ankle donor-site morbidity at 2-year follow-up. This tunnel-sparing technique may be considered a reasonable surgical option for patients with ACL insufficiency and clinically relevant concomitant AMRI. Level of evidence Level IV.

title: Acute rather than insidious symptom onset is associated with better postoperative outcomes after transtibial pull-out repair for medial meniscus posterior root tears.
abstract: Purpose To compare clinical and radiologic outcomes after transtibial pull-out repair for medial meniscus posterior root tears (MMPRTs) between patients with acute and insidious symptom onset. Methods Patients who underwent transtibial pull-out repair for MMPRTs between March 2022 and December 2023 and had a minimum 2-year follow-up were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were classified into an acute-onset group, defined by abrupt symptom onset during or immediately after a clear inciting knee incident, or an insidious-onset group, defined by gradually progressive symptoms without a definite precipitating event. Outcomes included patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and radiologic parameters. PROMs comprised the International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) and Lysholm scores, with minimal clinically important difference (MCID) achievement also assessed. Radiologic outcomes included Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) grade progression, meniscal extrusion and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) healing status. Results A total of 49 patients were included (28 acute-onset, 21 insidious-onset). Both groups showed significant improvement in IKDC and Lysholm scores, with similar MCID achievement rates. At final follow-up, the Acute Group had higher median IKDC scores than the Insidious Group (73.0 [66.8-79.0] vs. 67.0 [62.0-69.0]; p = 0.02) and Lysholm scores (76.0 [73.0-78.0] vs. 71.0 [70.0-74.0]; p < 0.01). KL-grade progression was less frequent in the Acute Group (1/28 [3.6%] vs. 8/21 [38.1%]; p < 0.01). Meniscal extrusion was also lower (3.3 [2.9-3.5] vs. 3.9 [3.1-4.0] mm; p = 0.01), although the absolute difference was small. MRI healing status did not differ between groups. Conclusion Acute-onset MMPRTs were associated with better postoperative functional outcomes and less radiologic progression than insidious-onset MMPRTs, although the clinical relevance of the small difference in meniscal extrusion remains uncertain. Therefore, symptom-onset pattern may provide potentially useful information for preoperative prognostic counselling, but this association should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in prospective studies. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Development and radiographic evaluation of a normalised guide-pin orientation abacus for anterior closing-wedge tibial osteotomy: Comparison with fixed-ratio and osteotomy-depth methods.
abstract: Purpose To develop a simplified mathematical model and abacus estimating anterior wedge resection height during slope-reducing tibial osteotomy from patient-specific guide-pin length and normalised guide-pin orientation, and to evaluate its accuracy under simulated radiographic conditions against fixed-ratio and osteotomy-depth methods. It was hypothesised that normalised guide-pin orientation would provide wedge-height estimates comparable to radiographic planning in both configurations. Methods Two hundred fifty-nine calibrated strict lateral knee radiographs from patients undergoing ACL reconstruction were retrospectively analysed in a single-centre radiographic simulation study. Supratuberosity and infratuberosity slope-reducing osteotomies were simulated with a standardised 10° correction, recording guide-pin length, orientation and corresponding anterior wedge height. Three models were compared: a trigonometric model with normalised mean angles, a fixed-ratio model and the osteotomy-depth method. Accuracy (mean absolute error, 90th percentile error) was assessed in-sample against radiographic reference measurements and confirmed by leave-one-out and five-fold cross-validation. Results Mean guide-pin orientation angles were 67.4° ± 6.0° (supratuberosity) and 110.6° ± 4.7° (infratuberosity). The normalised-angle model produced mean absolute errors of 0.45 ± 0.41 mm (95% CI, 0.40-0.50) and 0.88 ± 0.79 mm (95% CI, 0.78-0.98), with 90th percentile errors of 0.91 and 1.77 mm and Bland-Altman bias of -0.17 and -0.06 mm, lower than both comparator models. Estimation error was not significantly influenced by sex or baseline posterior tibial slope, though the cohort's imbalanced sex distribution (194 men, 65 women) limited power to detect smaller effects in women. Conclusion Within this model-development cohort, a patient-specific abacus based on guide-pin length and normalised guide-pin orientation produced low approximation errors under simulated radiographic conditions, without intraoperative radiographic calibration or complex calculations. These findings are exploratory and reflect in-sample performance; independent and clinical validation, including prospective intraoperative testing, are required before the method can be considered accurate, reproducible or ready for intraoperative use. Level of evidence Level IV, retrospective radiographic simulation/model-development study without clinical outcomes.

title: Side-Step Cutting Foot Biomechanics and Intrinsic Foot Muscle Sizes in People With Chronic Ankle Instability.
abstract: Introduction Lateral ankle sprains commonly occur during directional changes and often lead to chronic ankle instability (CAI) associated with altered movement patterns, muscle weakness and atrophy. This study aimed to compare foot joint biomechanics during cutting among individuals with CAI, copers, and uninjured controls and to explore the relationship between intrinsic foot muscle sizes and functional status. Methods Cross-sectional study. Sixty-nine recreationally active males (25.4 ± 4 years) were categorised by perceived instability and self-reported function. Ankle and foot joint kinematics and kinetics were assessed using a multi-segment foot model during 45° side-step cutting at a mean approach speed of 3.5 m·s -1 . Groups were compared using ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests, and continuous biomechanical data were analysed using statistical parametric or non-parametric mapping. Cross-sectional area and thickness of the abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis were recorded using ultrasound imaging. Muscle sizes were explored using general linear models, and correlations with questionnaire scores and physical examination outcomes were calculated. Results Foot joint kinematics and kinetics did not significantly differ between the groups. Individuals with CAI exhibited lower peak posterior ground reaction force than controls (mean difference: -6.2% of body weight, 95% CI: -11.9 to -0.4, p = 0.03). Statistical parametric mapping revealed lower posterior ground reaction forces from 22% to 46% of stance in CAI versus controls (p < 0.05). Intrinsic foot muscle sizes showed weak, statistically significant negative correlations with perceived instability scores (ρ = -0.31 to -0.36) and self-reported function scores (ρ = -0.26 to -0.33). Conclusion Despite pronounced sensory-perceptual impairments, individuals with CAI demonstrated few differences in foot joint biomechanics compared with copers and controls during a moderate-speed anticipated cutting task. Reduced braking forces may reflect altered deceleration strategies. These findings suggest the importance of assessing deceleration abilities in people with CAI and indicate a potential role of foot muscles in CAI-related functional outcomes. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05815576).

title: Prenatal Test Selection After First-Trimester Ultrasound Abnormalities Within a Centralized Genetic Counseling System in Japan.
abstract: This study evaluated the association between first-trimester ultrasound abnormalities and prenatal test selection within a centralized genetic counseling system in Japan. Advances in ultrasound screening and the increasing use of non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) have expanded prenatal testing options, increasing the complexity of test selection in pregnancies with abnormal ultrasound findings. This retrospective cohort study included 87 pregnant women referred for genetic counseling because of abnormal first-trimester ultrasound findings between July 2022 and December 2025. All patients received standardized prenatal genetic counseling. Clinical data were extracted from the medical records, and factors associated with the selection of invasive diagnostic testing were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression. Amniocentesis was selected in 41 pregnancies (47.1%), NIPT in 28 (32.2%), and no chromosomal testing in 18 (20.7%). Chromosomal abnormalities were identified in 15 of 41 pregnancies (36.6%) undergoing amniocentesis. Cystic hygroma was independently associated with the selection of invasive diagnostic testing (odds ratio [OR] 3.10, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.09-9.15), whereas increased nuchal translucency was negatively associated (OR 0.35, 95% CI 0.13-0.90). These findings suggest that the type of first-trimester ultrasound abnormality is associated with prenatal test selection. Our results highlight the importance of individualized genetic counseling when discussing prenatal testing options and residual uncertainty following abnormal ultrasound findings.

title: Inverse Association Between Regional Availability of Board-Certified Fellows of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society and Colorectal Cancer Mortality in Japan: An Ecological Analysis.
abstract: Aims We investigated the association between prefecture-level colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality and contributing factors, including the regional availability of Board-Certified Fellows of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society (BCFJGES), using publicly available data from all 47 Japanese prefectures. Methods and results This prefecture-level ecological cross-sectional study used publicly available national data from e-Stat, Cancer Statistics by the Japan National Cancer Center, and JGES records. The dependent variable was the CRC-specific age-standardized mortality rate (AMR) among individuals aged < 75 years in 2021. Independent variables (2010-2016) included CRC screening and follow-up rates, smoking, alcohol consumption, obesity, physical activity, diabetes prevalence, red meat consumption, mean income, gastroenterologist and BCFJGES density per 10 000 population, CRC stage distribution, and regional classification. Simple linear regression showed that smoking, alcohol consumption, and obesity were significantly associated with higher CRC AMR, whereas physical activity, income, and BCFJGES density were associated with lower AMR. Multiple linear regression confirmed independent associations for smoking (regression coefficient [ b ] = 0.213, p = 0.011), alcohol consumption ( b = 0.045, p = 0.003), physical activity ( b = -0.087, p = 0.024), and BCFJGES density ( b = -1.339, p < 0.001). The Pearson correlation coefficient between AMR and BCFJGES density was -0.482 ( p < 0.001). Conclusion Higher prefecture-level smoking and alcohol consumption were associated with higher CRC mortality, while higher physical activity and higher BCFJGES density were associated with lower mortality. Regional disparities in BCFJGES distribution across Japan may contribute to CRC mortality and warrant continued surveillance and policy attention.

title: Intragastric Pressure Required to Achieve Strong Extension of the Gastric Wall for Invasion Depth Assessment in Early Gastric Cancer: A Single-Center Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background and aims Previously, we developed a simple and accurate method to measure intragastric pressure (IP) using upper gastrointestinal endoscopy. This study prospectively characterized the IP at the first point of visually defined strong extension of the gastric wall and evaluated the diagnostic performance of the non-extension sign (NES) for assessing invasion depth in early gastric cancer (EGC). Methods This was a single-center prospective study. Consecutive patients with EGC scheduled for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy were enrolled. The patients underwent continued air insufflation until strong extension of the gastric wall occurred, at which point the IP was measured. Endoscopic assessment of invasion depth was then performed using the NES. Results Forty-six patients were enrolled; however, three were excluded, resulting in 43 patients included in the analysis. IP at the first point of strong extension of the gastric wall ranged from 5 to 20 mmHg; therefore, strong extension was achieved at an IP of 20 mmHg or less in all 43 patients. For the endoscopic diagnosis of the depth of invasion in EGC using the NES, this yielded a sensitivity of 80% (95% confidence interval (CI), 37.6%-96.4%), a specificity of 100% (95% CI, 90.8%-100%), and a diagnostic accuracy of 98% (95% CI, 87.9-99.6). No procedure-related adverse events were observed. Conclusions IP at the first point of visually defined strong extension of the gastric wall ranged from 5 to 20 mmHg among technically evaluable patients. NES assessment showed high specificity and diagnostic accuracy, with no adverse events observed. Trial Registration: UMIN 000046904.

title: Pulmonary Involvement in Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia: A Structured Diagnostic Approach to Diffuse Infiltrates-A Case Report.
abstract: Pulmonary abnormalities in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) usually reflect infection, pleural effusion, treatment toxicity, second malignancy, or Richter transformation. Leukemic pulmonary infiltration is underrecognized and radiologically heterogeneous. A 64-year-old man with CLL developed dyspnea, cough, and bilateral basal crazy-paving opacities on high-resolution computed tomography. Bronchoalveolar lavage showed lymphocytosis and a CD5-positive monoclonal B-cell population. Transbronchial lung cryobiopsy supported CLL infiltration and argued against mantle-cell lymphoma or transformation. Obinutuzumab plus venetoclax was followed by clinical improvement and regression of the interstitial lung opacities on follow-up imaging. This case supports combining BAL flow cytometry with tissue confirmation in this unusual pulmonary presentation. Trial Registration: The authors have confirmed clinical trial registration is not needed for this submission.

title: Abbreviated MRI and Ultrafast MRI of the Breast.
abstract: Detection of breast cancer in MRI requires fast, dynamic contrast enhanced (DCE) imaging covering the immediate post-contrast phase, that is, the first 60 s after contrast injection. This ensures selective depiction of invasive cancer as well as DCIS against an otherwise dark background, that is, before background parenchymal enhancement (BPE) can set in. Thus, breast MRI requires not only high spatial, but also high temporal resolution. Both, abbreviated breast MRI (AB-MRI) as well as ultrafast breast MRI (UF-MRI), exploit the fact that enhancement of cancers versus their non-cancerous background differs most in the immediate post-contrast phase. Beyond this, however, AB-MRI and UF-MRI are unrelated: AB-MRI is a novel MRI paradigm; UF-MRI is a novel MRI pulse sequence that allows time-resolved imaging of the immediate post-contrast phase. AB-MRI is an umbrella term for lean, streamlined MRI protocols designed to answer specific clinical questions. Compared with "all-purpose" full-protocol MRI, AB-MRI allows a substantial reduction of acquisition time. The first proposed use case of AB-MRI was for breast cancer screening, to reduce cost, and thus improve access and tolerability. It had been termed "FAST," short for "first post-contrast subtracted imaging," because it truncated the breast MRI acquisition protocol after one post-contrast scan covering the immediate post-contrast phase. Around the same time, UF-MRI was inaugurated. This may have caused the misunderstanding that both would represent different positions on the same line of development, with "ultrafast" being even faster than "FAST." AB-MRI protocols can be categorized into short and abridged protocols. Short protocols concentrate on the pre- and immediate post-contrast phase, either by regular DCE-MRI, or by UF-MRI. Abridged protocols add carefully selected scans, for example, T2-weighted and/or post-contrast scans. This review aims at clarifying the definitions and respective concepts of AB-MRI and UF-MRI, and to summarize the current evidence regarding the respective utility for breast cancer diagnosis.

title: Evaluation of Pre-Operative Cartilage and Meniscus Ultrashort Echo Time T2* as Biomarkers of Long-Term Clinical Outcomes Following Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction.
abstract: Ultrashort echo time T2* (UTE-T2*) mapping is sensitive to the composition of deep cartilage and menisci. UTE-T2* elevations are common after anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries, but their long-term prognostic importance is unknown. Higher pre-operative UTE-T2* values will associate with greater symptoms and radiographic knee osteoarthritis (KOA) at long-term follow-up. Retrospective longitudinal cohort study using prospectively acquired baseline MRI and follow-up clinical outcomes. Twenty-two participants (13 female, mean [SD] age: 29 [9] years) with ACL reconstruction (ACLR). 3T, 3D acquisition-weighted stack of spirals. Pre-operative UTE-T2* maps from participants who underwent ACLR (2009-2012) were compared to 11-year follow-up Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Scores (KOOS), the Marx Activity Rating Scale scores, and radiographs. Linear regression models assessed relationships between pre-operative cartilage and meniscus UTE-T2* and follow-up KOOS Symptoms or Marx scores. Mann-Whitney U-tests assessed differences in pre-operative UTE-T2* by radiographic KOA status (Kellgren-Lawrence grade ≥ 2). two-sided α < 0.05. KOOS and Marx scores were available for 22 participants at a median of 11.3 years (range: 10.3-12.4) after ACLR; radiographs were available for 11 participants. After adjustment for meniscus tear status, higher pre-operative UTE-T2* values in the deep medial femoral cartilage and medial meniscus were associated with worse KOOS Symptoms at 11 years (adjusted R2 = 0.146-0.332). Higher femoral cartilage UTE-T2* trended with lower Marx scores (adjusted R2 = 0.208, p = 0.056), while higher posterior meniscus UTE-T2* was associated with higher Marx scores (adjusted R2 = 0.308). In the small radiographic subset, median pre-operative posterior meniscus UTE-T2* was 69% higher in patients with radiographic KOA. Pre-operative UTE-T2* in medial compartment cartilage and menisci were associated with knee symptoms and activity levels 11 years after ACLR. These findings support the potential utility of elevated cartilage and meniscus UTE-T2* as markers of pre-osteoarthritis reflecting symptomatic and structural KOA risk after ACLR. Level 3. Stage 3 Diagnostic Thinking.

title: Slice-Wise Quality Assessment of High b Value Breast DWI via Deep Learning-Based Artifact Detection.
abstract: Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) can support lesion detection and characterization in breast MRI. Therefore, DWI is increasingly being incorporated into breast MRI protocols to address some of the shortcomings of routine clinical breast MRI. However, especially high b value DWI can be prone to intensity artifacts that can affect diagnostic image assessment. To detect hyper- and hypointense artifacts on high b value DWI (b = 1500 s/mm2) using deep learning, employing either a binary classification (artifact presence) or a multiclass classification (artifact intensity) approach on a slice-wise dataset. Retrospective. 11,806 DWI slices were acquired from 156 examinations performed on female patients between 2022 and mid-2023. For both hyper- and hypointense artifact classification, the slices were split into test, validation, and holdout test set with 8164/1806/1836 and 8164/1820/1822 slices in these sets respectively. 3 T spin-echo planar diffusion-weighted sequence with b values: 50, 750, and 1500 s/mm2. Three convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures (DenseNet121, ResNet18, and SEResNet50) were trained for binary classification of hyper- and hypointense artifacts on slice-wise labeled data. The best performing model (DenseNet121) was applied to an independent holdout test set and further trained separately for multiclass classification. Performance of the networks was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and under the precision recall curve (AUPRC). Radiologist evaluated bounding box positions on a 5-point Likert-like scale across 150 slices for validation and 200 slices for the holdout test set, derived from the network's Grad-CAM heatmaps. DenseNet121 achieved AUROCs of 0.91 and 0.95 for hyper- and hypointense artifact detection, respectively, and weighted AUROCs of 0.84 and 0.90 for multiclass classification on single-slice high b value diffusion-weighted images, achieving mean scores of 3.52 ± 0.81 for hyperintense artifacts and 3.62 ± 0.65 for hypointense artifacts. Hyper- and hypointense artifact detection in slice-wise breast DWI MRI dataset (b = 1500 s/mm2) using CNNs, particularly DenseNet121, suggests potential reliability and requires further validation. 3. Stage 3.

title: MR Cytometry of Microstructural Changes in Breast Cancer: Association With Treatment Response and Prognosis.
abstract: Background Although MR cytometry can probe microstructural features, the longitudinal trajectories of these changes during neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) and their association with treatment response and prognosis remain poorly defined. Purpose To characterize longitudinal changes in NAC-associated cellular microstructural properties and evaluate microstructural parameters for predicting pathologic complete response (pCR) and disease-free survival (DFS) in breast cancer. Study type Prospective. Population 194 patients with invasive breast cancer underwent 713 MRI examinations. Field strength/sequence 3.0 T, oscillating gradient spin-echo (OGSE) and pulsed gradient spin-echo (PGSE) sequences. Assessment MR cytometry was acquired at four time-points: pretreatment, early, mid-, and late treatment. Microstructural parameters were estimated using the IMPULSED (imaging microstructural parameters using limited spectrally edited diffusion) model. Microstructural parameters were compared with histopathologic measurements. Statistical tests Generalized estimating equations, logistic regression, bootstrap resampling, the DeLong test with Bonferroni correction, Cox proportional hazards regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test, the C-index, and the Pearson correlation coefficient were performed. p < 0.05 was significant. Results Four logistic regression models were developed for predicting pCR, based on molecular subtype alone or combined with diameter at Time 1, ADC 50Hz at Time 2, or cellularity at Time 2. The clinicopathological-cellularity model achieved the best performance in predicting pCR (AUC = 0.89). For DFS, a Cox model incorporating ER status, HER2 status, cT stage, cN stage, and extracellular diffusivity at Time 1 yielded a C-index of 0.81; patients stratified by the median risk score into low- and high-risk groups differed significantly in DFS. Extracellular diffusion was positively correlated with pathologic stroma fraction (r = 0.56). Data conclusion MR cytometry demonstrated longitudinal microstructural alterations during NAC and shows potential for predicting pCR and stratifying patients by DFS risk in breast cancer patients. Level of evidence: 1 Technical efficacy Stage 2.

title: MRI-Based 2.5D Multi-Instance Deep Learning for Differentiating Pathological Subtypes of Brain Metastases From Lung Cancer.
abstract: Background Distinct treatment strategies for small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases require accurate noninvasive subtyping. Purpose To develop and externally validate a biparametric MRI-based 2.5D multi-instance learning (MIL) deep learning (DL) model for discriminating SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases, with performance compared against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models. Study type Retrospective. Population This study included 366 patients from four institutions. Center 1 provided the training set (n = 199; mean age, 63.88 ± 10.79 years; 72.36% male) and an internal tuning set (n = 85; mean age, 64.73 ± 9.53 years; 67.06% male). Centers 2-4 were pooled into a single external test set (n = 82; mean age, 62.26 ± 10.60 years; 63.41% male). Field strength/sequence 1.5 T and 3.0 T; contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery imaging. Assessment The 2.5D-MIL model was benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models and evaluated on internal tuning and pooled external test sets. Statistical tests Shapiro-Wilk, Student's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and DeLong tests were used. Performance measures included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals and classification and calibration metrics. Statistical significance was defined as two-sided p < 0.05. Results In the internal tuning set, AUCs were 0.842 (2.5D-MIL), 0.740 (clinical), 0.710 (radiomics), and 0.747 (3D-DL). In the external test set, AUCs were 0.826 (2.5D-MIL), 0.826 (clinical), 0.696 (radiomics), and 0.664 (3D-DL). Differences between 2.5D-MIL and the clinical (p = 1.000), radiomics (p = 0.139), and 3D-DL (p = 0.119) models were not significant. Data conclusion The MRI-based 2.5D-MIL model showed potential for noninvasive differentiation of SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases. Larger prospective studies are needed before clinical use. Evidence level 3. Technical efficacy Stage 2.

title: Quantitative UTE MRI Differences in the Meniscus Following ACL Reconstruction: A Prospective Cohort Study Using 3D Ultrashort Echo Time Adiabatic T1rho and Magnetization Transfer Imaging.
abstract: Background ACLR is associated with altered joint loading and increased risk of post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Conventional MRI has limited sensitivity to early meniscal differences because of short-T2 signal decay and magic-angle effects. Purpose To evaluate whether 3D ultrashort echo time imaging-based adiabatic T1rho (UTE-Adiab-T1rho) and ultrashort echo time imaging-based macromolecular fraction (UTE-MMF) identify regional quantitative MRI differences after ACLR. Study type Prospective longitudinal cohort study. Population 30 control scans, 19 ACLR scans at 6-12 months, and 13 ACLR scans at 12+ months were analyzed. Mean ages were 34.5, 34.5, and 37.2 years; female/male counts were 15/15, 9/10, and 8/5. Field strength/sequence Participants underwent 3-T knee MRI with 3D fat-saturated UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE magnetization transfer sequences. Assessment UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF maps were generated with single-component exponential and two-pool magnetization transfer models. Values were extracted from four meniscal regions of interest by a blinded reader, with blinded redelineation in a subset. Patient-reported outcomes included International Knee Documentation Committee, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score, and Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index scores. Statistical tests Linear mixed-effects models accounted for repeated observations. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction was applied. Results UTE-Adiab-T1rho showed significant group (q = 0.001) and region (q < 0.001) effects. Compared with controls, UTE-Adiab-T1rho was higher in LAM at 6-12 months (+5.60 ms; q = 0.035) and 12+ months (+7.09 ms; q = 0.028), and in LPM at 12+ months (+6.35 ms; q = 0.035). UTE-MMF showed significant group (q = 0.041) and region (q < 0.001) effects. LPM UTE-MMF was lower than controls at 6-12 months (-3.56 percentage points; q = 0.028) and 12+ months (-3.10 percentage points; q = 0.049). No 6-12 versus 12+ month MRI or PROM contrast survived FDR correction. MRI-PROM associations were not FDR-significant (all q ≥ 0.383). Data conclusion UTE-Adiab-T1rho and UTE-MMF mapping identified regional MRI differences after ACLR. Pairwise differences were concentrated in lateral regions, but corrected group-by-region interactions were not significant. PROMs were worse after ACLR but did not differ between postoperative windows after correction. Evidence level 2. Technical efficacy stage 2.

title: Intraoperative Application of the PRAETORIAN Score to Predict Optimal Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Placement.
abstract: Background The PRAETORIAN score (PS) estimates the risk of defibrillation failure after subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) implantation based on postoperative chest radiography in the standing position. However, the usefulness of assessing the PS in the supine position intraoperatively has not yet been established. Methods We evaluated conventional (standing) and intraoperative supine PS in 124 consecutive Japanese patients undergoing S-ICD implantation. Changes between conventional and supine PS values were analyzed in two ways: (1) the presence of any difference in the absolute PS values regardless of the risk category, and (2) changes in clinically relevant risk categories for conversion failure (low, intermediate, or high risk). Predictors of discordance between the two assessments were also investigated. Results The median conventional PS was 30; 116 and 8 patients were classified as having low and intermediate risk of conversion failure, respectively. Numerical differences between the conventional and supine PS values were observed in 13 patients. However, clinically meaningful risk reclassification occurred in only two patients, suggesting that intraoperative supine PS assessment may underestimate PRAETORIAN score-based risk classification in a small subset of patients. Among patients with numerical PS changes, supine PS was significantly lower than conventional PS. An elevated BMI was strongly associated with PS discordance. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a BMI cutoff of 25.6 kg/m 2 for discriminating patients with numerical PS discordance. Conclusions Intraoperative supine PS assessment shows excellent concordance with conventional standing PS and may provide a practical tool for confirming appropriate system positioning in most Japanese patients.

title: Development and Validation of an Interpretable Deep Learning Model for Automated Kellgren-Lawrence Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis Using X-Ray Imaging.
abstract: Accurate and reproducible Kellgren-Lawrence grading of radiographic knee osteoarthritis remains challenging, particularly for intermediate grades and anatomically heterogeneous compartments. We present X-VIG, an interpretable deep learning framework integrating paired anteroposterior and lateral knee radiographs via view-specific backbones with deformable convolutions, attention-based feature fusion, and dual classification-regression optimization aligned with five-grade clinical practice. Grad-CAM++ visualizations enhance model transparency and support clinical interpretation. In a retrospective cohort (n = 229) with consensus reference-standard KL labels established by double-blinded expert review and patient-level splitting (70%/30%), X-VIG achieved AUCs of 0.9646-0.9945 across five anatomical subregions. Multimodal fusion yielded a mean AUC gain of 5.6 percentage points over single-view models. In a reader study of 50 held-out patients comprising 100 individual radiographs, X-VIG outperformed junior radiologists, matched or surpassed senior performance in most subregions, and reduced reading time by 82% (27 s per case). These results position X-VIG as a credible second reader for standardizing the reporting of knee osteoarthritis in routine clinical workflows.

title: Not All Cams Are Equal: MRI-Based Statistical Shape Modeling Reveals High Variability in Cam Shape in a Large FAI Cohort.
abstract: Evidence indicates that alpha angle (AA) is inadequate for describing cam morphology, contributing to poor patient selection and clinical outcomes for cam-type femoroacetabular impingement syndrome (FAI). While techniques such as statistical shape modeling (SSM) have advanced knowledge of 3D femoral morphology, many studies utilize computed tomography, which incurs ionizing radiation, or small sample sizes, limiting clinical implementation and generalization. Here, we conducted SSM using MRI-derived 3D femur models from a large cohort of FAI patients to explore: (1) What proximal femur features drive shape variability? (2) What variability exists within the area of the cam deformity? (3) Are shape modes correlated to AA, age, sex, and BMI? 103 FAI patients were enrolled (µ ± σ): Age (29.9 ± 12.1 Years), BMI (24.6 ± 4.8), AA (60.3° ± 9.8), Female/Male (75/28). Shape modes were determined through principal component analysis. Relationships between shape modes and AA, age, and BMI were evaluated through linear regression. Sex differences were analyzed using linear discriminant analysis. Thirteen modes explained 91.0% of femoral shape variance, with the first six modes explaining 82.2%, four of which were associated with the cam deformity region. No relationship was found between any mode versus AA, BMI, or age. Sex-based shape differences were primarily captured by the first mode. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: The proximal femur in cam-type FAI patients demonstrated substantial regional shape variability, with cam-related morphology distributed across multiple independent modes rather than a single uniform deformity pattern. Sex was a major driver of proximal femoral shape variation. These findings may inform morphology-based classification, outcome analysis, and patient-specific surgical planning.

title: Preoperative 7 T 3D Meniscal T2* Mapping Correlates With Postoperative Extrusion After Medial Meniscus Posterior Root Tear Repair.
abstract: Medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT) repairs stabilize root attachment and yield improved clinical outcomes, yet many patients develop persistent meniscal extrusion and osteoarthritis. This study evaluates menisci in MMPRT patients using 3D T2* mapping and assesses T2* correlation with medial meniscal extrusion. Patients underwent 7 T knee MRI before root tear repair and again at 6-month postoperative follow-up. Age- and gender-matched controls were scanned once. The protocol included clinical turbo-spin-echo sequences and a quantitative 3D GRE sequence, used to calculate T2* mapping of the menisci. Pre- and postrepair meniscal extrusion was measured on coronal T2-weighted images by two independent radiologists. Twenty-five patients (mean age 53 ± 8 years) and nine controls (51 ± 11 years) were included. Repairs were intact on follow-up MRI in all patients. T2* values were significantly elevated in patients both pre- and postrepair compared with controls across medial and lateral meniscal subregions. Medial meniscal extrusion increased from 3.7 ± 1.1 mm at baseline to 4.9 ± 1.5 mm (p = 0.002), postoperatively. Prerepair meniscal T2* strongly correlated with postrepair extrusion (ρ = 0.765; p < 0.001). High-resolution 3D T2* mapping at 7 T revealed persistently elevated T2* values after MMPRT repair, consistent with ongoing collagen fiber disorganization. Prerepair T2* values were strongly correlated with early postrepair meniscal extrusion despite MRI-intact repairs, indicating that preoperative tissue quality is associated with postoperative outcomes. These findings support quantitative T2* mapping as a prognostic imaging biomarker that complements conventional morphologic MRI in the evaluation of MMPRTs.

title: Circumferential Meniscal Extrusion Mapping Using Radial Multiplanar Reconstructions.
abstract: Meniscal extrusion is a marker of meniscal dysfunction and has been associated with osteoarthritis progression. Assessment is typically performed on a single coronal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) slice, but this method may miss the location of maximal circumferential displacement. We developed an extrusion mapping technique using radially oriented multiplanar reconstruction (rMPR) images from high-resolution 3D MRI to enable circumferential meniscal position measurements perpendicular to the tibial margin. Extrusion was measured by three independent readers on rMPR images generated from non-fat-saturated 3D fast spin-echo MRI in 20 patients stratified by meniscal tear and extrusion status. Intrareader and interreader measurement variabilities were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), 95% repeatability coefficient (RC; intrareader), and 95% reproducibility coefficient (RDC; interreader). Corresponding rMPR and standard 2D coronal midbody extrusion measurements were compared. Intrareader variability was low, with a mean within-meniscus within-angle standard deviation (SD) of 0.2 mm and mean RC of 0.6 mm. Interreader variability was also low, with a mean within-meniscus within-angle SD of 0.5 mm and mean RDC of 1.4 mm. At the midbody, there was 98% concordance for extrusion classification between rMPR and 2D coronal measurements within the interreader RDC (1.4 mm). Exploratory regional analysis suggested different extrusion patterns between medial and lateral menisci and between torn and intact menisci. These findings suggest that circumferential meniscal extrusion mapping using rMPR images from 3D knee MRI is feasible, with low intrareader and interreader measurement variabilities. This framework enables regional characterization of meniscal displacement and should support future investigations of meniscus-osteoarthritis relationships. STATEMENT OF CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Meniscus extrusion circumferential mapping using radially oriented multiplanar reconstruction images is feasible and consistent across readers and allows a more complete assessment of meniscal position, which may be valuable for further investigation of meniscal injury and osteoarthritis.

title: Human immunodeficiency virus infection mimicking very early onset inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract: Very early onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO-IBD), defined as diagnosis before 6 years of age, is often associated with immune dysregulation and monogenic etiologies; however, infectious mimics may be overlooked in low-prevalence regions. We report a 4-year-old male with poor weight gain, intermittent diarrhea, elevated fecal calprotectin, and persistently elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Endoscopy showed diffuse friable colonic mucosa, and biopsies demonstrated focal active colitis with mild crypt distortion. He was diagnosed with VEO-IBD and treated with mesalamine, infliximab, adalimumab, and upadacitinib, with incomplete response. At age 7, he was hospitalized with fever, cytopenias, and pulmonary infiltrates; human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) testing was positive, with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cytomegalovirus viremia. After discontinuing immunosuppression and initiating antiretroviral therapy, gastrointestinal symptoms and inflammatory markers improved. HIV-associated colitis can closely mimic VEO-IBD, and progressive lymphopenia should prompt evaluation for secondary immunodeficiency.

title: Defining the Clinical Indication for Real-Time Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound in Breast Lesions with Low Suspicion of Malignancy.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether real-time artificial intelligence (AI) breast ultrasound (US) can identify a subgroup of breast imaging reporting and data system (BI-RADS) category 4A lesions without suspicious mammographic (MMG) findings in whom unnecessary biopsy may be safely avoided. Methods This retrospective analysis of single-center biopsy registry included 641 consecutive US BI-RADS 4A lesions that underwent vacuum-assisted breast biopsy. Before conducting biopsy, the lesions were reassessed using a real-time AI US system (CadAI-B®), and MMG findings were classified as suspicious or non-suspicious based on formal reports. Seven prespecified biopsy-decision strategies were evaluated, including 3 AI-only strategies, 3 mammography-gated AI strategies, and the current standard strategy of biopsy all BI-RADS 4A lesions. The primary outcomes were biopsy reduction rate, missed cancers, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy, with final pathology as the reference standard. Results Among 641 cases of US BI-RADS 4A lesions, 26 cases of malignancies (4.1%) were identified, including 14 cases of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), 11 cases of invasive ductal carcinomas, and 1 case of apocrine carcinoma. AI reassigned 289 cases of lesions (45.1%) to BI-RADS categories 1-3. AI-only biopsy-deferral strategies missed 30.8% and 38.5% of malignancies when biopsy was deferred for AI BI-RADS ≤2 and ≤3 lesions, respectively, with DCIS accounting for most missed cancers. In contrast, among lesions without suspicious MMG findings, no malignancies were observed in AI BI-RADS 1-3 lesions. The sequential strategy of deferring biopsy only for lesions with AI BI-RADS ≤3 and non-suspicious MMG findings reduced biopsies by 43.5% (279/641) while maintaining 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 87.1-100.0%) and increasing specificity to 45.4% (95% CI, 41.4-49.4%). Conclusion Real-time AI breast US alone could not safely support biopsy deferral in US BI-RADS 4A lesions. However, after suspicious MMG findings had been excluded, AI identified a low-risk subgroup in whom unnecessary biopsy could be substantially reduced without compromising cancer detection. These findings suggest that the clinical utility of real-time AI breast US lies in patients without suspicious MMG findings. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Value of Multimodal Ultrasound Imaging With Super-Resolution in the Differential Diagnosis of Benign and Malignant Superficial Lymph Nodes: A Dual-Center Prospective Study.
abstract: Objectives Accurate differential diagnosis of benign and malignant superficial lymph nodes (LNs) is critical for clinical management. The objectives of this study were to explore the feasibility and clinical value of super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) in the differential diagnosis of superficial lymphadenopathy and to establish and validate a multimodal ultrasound diagnostic model based on conventional ultrasound (US), contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), and SRUS, so as to improve the accuracy of distinguishing benign from malignant superficial LNs in clinical practice. Methods A total of 200 LNs from 165 patients with superficial lymphadenectasis were prospectively enrolled from two medical centers. All patients underwent conventional US, CEUS, and SRUS imaging. Predictive models were constructed based on the conventional US, CEUS, and SRUS features in the training cohort, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were calculated to evaluate their predictive performance in the external validation cohort. Results The training cohort comprised 117 patients with a total of 140 LNs including 46 benign and 94 malignant lesions. The validation cohort included 48 patients with 60 LNs in total, with 21 benign and 39 malignant lesions. Among the models constructed based on the training cohort, the SRUS model exhibited significantly superior diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.822) to the conventional US and CEUS models (P < .05). The combined model, integrating all three modalities, achieved an AUC of 0.892 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.833-0.952) in the training cohort and 0.890 (95% CI: 0.791-0.990) in the external validation cohort, demonstrating excellent and stable diagnostic performance. Conclusion SRUS provides crucial imaging evidence for the non-invasive qualitative evaluation of LNs. The multimodal diagnostic model incorporating the features of US, CEUS, and SRUS can significantly improve the accuracy of distinguishing benign from malignant LNs.

title: ACR TI-RADS Modified by CEUS Features and Nodule Location for Diagnosis and Biopsy Decision in Thyroid Nodules of TR4 or Higher.
abstract: Objectives To develop a modified American College of Radiology (ACR) thyroid imaging, reporting and data system (TI-RADS) incorporating contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) features and nodule location to improve diagnostic performance and fine-needle aspiration (FNA) recommendations for ACR TR4 or higher thyroid nodules. Methods This prospective study enrolled patients who underwent ultrasound and CEUS at 3 hospitals between June 2024 and January 2026. CEUS and location features were analyzed using multivariable logistic regression to construct the modified system. Diagnostic performance and biopsy recommendation efficiency were compared with ACR TI-RADS. Results Four hundred and eight patients with 442 nodules were included. Independent predictors included enhancement intensity, enhancement direction, ring enhancement, enhancement area and nodule location. In the training set (n = 334), the modified system achieved higher AUC and sensitivity than ACR TI-RADS (AUC: 0.90 [95% CI: 0.86-0.93] versus 0.75 [95% CI: 0.71-0.79]; sensitivity: 88.5% versus 60.3%; p < .01), higher accuracy of malignant nodule biopsies (AMB: 67.1% versus 49.4%), lower unnecessary biopsy rate (UBR: 32.9% versus 50.6%), and lower biopsy rate of benign nodules (BRB: 20.8% versus 31.2%), with no unsafe downgrading. Similar results were observed in the temporal validation set (n = 108): AUC 0.95 (95% CI: 0.90-0.99) versus 0.73 (95% CI: 0.66-0.79); sensitivity 87.0% versus 49.3%; AMB 83.3% versus 53.3%; UBR 16.7% versus 46.7%, and BRB 5.1% versus 17.9%. Conclusions A modified ACR TI-RADS integrating CEUS features and nodule location improved diagnostic performance and FNA recommendations for ACR TR4 or higher nodules. Pending external validation, this system may provide a practical approach for refining risk stratification and reducing unnecessary biopsies.

title: Multiparametric Ultrasound in Budd-Chiari Syndrome: From Venous Outflow Obstruction to Microcirculatory Dysfunction.
abstract: Budd-Chiari syndrome (BCS) is a rare and potentially severe disorder of hepatic venous outflow with a heterogeneous anatomical and etiological spectrum. Obstruction may range from focal or segmental involvement of a single hepatic vein to multifocal hepatic venous disease with inferior vena cava (IVC) involvement. Although BCS is traditionally diagnosed by demonstrating macroscopic venous obstruction, its clinical severity also depends on the resulting changes in sinusoidal pressure, hepatic perfusion, collateral circulation, and the intrahepatic microcirculation. Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), although less common than myeloproliferative neoplasms as an underlying cause of BCS, represents a particularly severe prothrombotic model in which macrovascular thrombosis may coexist with systemic vascular and microcirculatory abnormalities. The purpose of the study is to provide a pathophysiology-oriented review of BCS, with emphasis on the relationship between hepatic venous outflow obstruction, altered hepatic hemodynamics, tissue perfusion, microcirculatory dysfunction, and the complementary role of conventional and advanced imaging techniques, using PNH as a model of severe thrombotic BCS. A narrative literature review was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE and related biomedical databases for publications from January 2000 to March 2026, supplemented by relevant earlier landmark studies. Literature addressing the etiology and pathophysiology of BCS, PNH-associated thrombosis, hepatic hemodynamics, conventional and advanced ultrasound techniques, computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) was reviewed. Particular attention was given to Doppler ultrasound, contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), parametric perfusion imaging, microvascular flow imaging, and elastography. BCS results from a broad spectrum of primary and secondary causes, including myeloproliferative neoplasms, PNH, inherited and acquired thrombophilia, malignancy, trauma, and iatrogenic conditions. The anatomical extent and duration of venous obstruction determine the degree of sinusoidal hypertension, hepatic congestion, redistribution of portal and arterial flow, and development of intrahepatic collateral pathways. Conventional Doppler ultrasound remains the foundation of diagnosis and provides assessment of venous patency, the extent of obstruction, waveform abnormalities, portal and arterial hemodynamics, and collateral circulation. CEUS and parametric perfusion imaging provide complementary information regarding regional and temporal hepatic perfusion, while microvascular flow imaging may demonstrate slow residual flow and small collateral pathways not readily visualized with conventional Doppler. Elastography provides additional information regarding congestion-related tissue stiffness and chronic remodeling. CT and MRI remain essential for comprehensive anatomical characterization, identification of secondary causes, assessment of parenchymal complications, and treatment planning. BCS should be regarded as a dynamic disorder of hepatic circulation rather than solely as an anatomical abnormality of the hepatic veins or IVC. A multiparametric imaging approach integrating morphology, macrovascular hemodynamics, tissue perfusion, microvascular flow, and tissue mechanics may provide a more comprehensive assessment of disease phenotype and treatment response than assessment of venous patency alone. PNH provides a particularly informative model for understanding the interaction between macrovascular thrombosis and microcirculatory dysfunction. However, advanced ultrasound techniques remain complementary and require further prospective validation, standardization, and correlation with hemodynamic measurements, hepatic functional reserve, and clinical outcomes.

title: Preoperative varus ≥10° does not compromise outcome after medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty, whereas postoperative joint-line convergence angle and insert thickness influence functional results: A matched-pair analysis.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate functional outcomes and implant survival following medial unicompartmental knee arthroplasty (UKA) in patients with anteromedial osteoarthritis and preoperative varus deformity ≥10° and to identify postoperative alignment thresholds that optimize outcomes. Methods Patients with preoperative varus ≥10° who underwent medial mobile-bearing UKA were retrospectively analysed and matched 1:1 to knees with preoperative varus <10°, yielding 132 pairs (264 knees) with similar baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were revision rates and the Oxford Knee Score (OKS). Full-length standing radiographs were used to measure the hip-knee-ankle angle (HKA), joint-line convergence angle (JLCA), extra-articular deformity (EAD), mechanical medial proximal tibial angle (mMPTA), mechanical lateral distal femoral angle (mLDFA) and joint-line obliquity (JLO) and determine functional knee phenotypes. Univariate curve-adjusted regression assessed the influence of alignment on OKS, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis defined the alignment range within which the Patient-Acceptable Symptomatic State (PASS) was achieved. Results At a mean follow-up of 10.1 ± 3.3 years, OKS did not differ between groups (40.6 ± 8.0 vs. 38.8 ± 5.7, n.s.), nor did revision-free survival (92.3% vs. 90.2% at 10 years, p = 0.618). In knees with preoperative varus ≥10°, postoperative JLCA correlated with OKS (R 2 = 0.43, p < 0.001), whereas HKA, EAD, mMPTA, mLDFA and JLO showed no association (p > 0.05). JLCA outside 0°-5° varus yielded inferior OKS (35.6 ± 11.0 vs. 42.4 ± 6.2, p = 0.022) and lower PASS achievement (33% vs. 70%, p = 0.011). Insert thickness ≥7 mm was associated with lower OKS (32.1 ± 12.1 vs. 41.2 ± 5.9, p = 0.004) and reduced PASS (30% vs. 81%, p = 0.046). Conclusions Medial UKA in knees with preoperative varus deformity ≥10° achieved functional outcomes and implant survival comparable to matched knees with varus <10°, provided postoperative JLCA is restored to 0°-5° varus and excessive insert thickness is avoided. Intraoperative insert upsizing should prompt reassessment for ligamentous insufficiency or compartment overstuffing. Level of evidence Level III.

title: Greater three-dimensional cam burden and superolateral location are associated with end-stage hip osteoarthritis: A retrospective comparative study.
abstract: Purpose Cam-type femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is a recognised structural contributor to primary hip osteoarthritis (OA), yet many cam-positive hips do not progress to radiographic joint failure. This study aimed to compare three-dimensional cam morphology and lesion location between cam-positive hips with end-stage primary osteoarthritis and cam-positive, non-arthritic hips in an elderly fracture cohort. Methods Hospital records and imaging archives from January 2020 to January 2026 were retrospectively reviewed at a single centre. The OA group comprised patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for primary OA, and the fracture group comprised patients aged ≥ 65 years treated for intertrochanteric or subtrochanteric femoral fractures without radiographic OA. Cam morphology was characterised using radial CT-based alpha angle, three-dimensional cam volume, cam/head volume ratio, and clock-face-based lesion location. Group comparisons, receiver operating characteristic analyses, correlation testing, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Results A total of 438 cam-positive hips were included (126 OA and 312 fracture). OA hips demonstrated higher alpha angles (72.44° ± 5.94° vs. 62.45° ± 5.07°), larger cam volumes (5274.77 ± 1353.26 mm 3 vs. 3215.20 ± 1524.84 mm 3 ), higher cam/head ratios (8.61% ± 2.02% vs. 6.35% ± 1.97%), and more superolateral lesions (52.4% vs. 36.2% anterior in the fracture group) (all p < 0.001). Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analyses identified cohort-specific discriminatory values of 66° for alpha angle (AUC, 0.884), 4421 mm 3 for cam volume (AUC, 0.839), and 6.4% for the cam-to-head volume ratio (AUC, 0.791). In multivariable analyses using continuous morphology measures, higher alpha angle, greater cam volume, higher cam-to-head volume ratio, and superolateral lesion location were associated with end-stage OA-group membership. Conclusions Compared with non-arthritic cam-positive hips in an elderly fracture cohort, end-stage primary OA hips had greater three-dimensional cam burden, with lesions more often located superolaterally. These retrospective associations do not establish longitudinal progression, causality, or individual prognosis. Study design Retrospective comparative study. Level of evidence Level III, study of a non-consecutive patients, study of diagnostic test.

title: Artificial intelligence across the continuum of care for the aging musculoskeletal patient: From longitudinal phenotyping to personalized surgery and recovery monitoring.
abstract: Musculoskeletal care is being reshaped by population aging, multimorbidity, frailty, osteoporosis, sarcopenia, polypharmacy and increasing vulnerability to postoperative loss of independence. Artificial intelligence (AI) has entered orthopaedic research, but its clinical translation remains constrained. Many models address isolated diagnostic, imaging or short-term prediction tasks rather than the longitudinal care trajectories that determine outcomes in older musculoskeletal patients. The central limitation is therefore not simply whether older adults are represented in datasets, but whether AI systems are valid across the continuum of geriatric orthopaedic care. This review argues for a transition from task-specific orthopaedic AI toward continuum-of-care AI for the aging musculoskeletal patient. Upstream, radiomics, longitudinal osteoarthritis phenotyping, opportunistic computed tomography (CT)-based skeletal assessment and AI-augmented dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) modelling may improve prediction of disease progression, fracture risk, treatment failure and surgical timing. At the point of intervention, AI-assisted arthroplasty planning may help move total knee arthroplasty from generic alignment targets toward phenotype-specific reconstruction strategies that account for constitutional alignment, bone morphology, ligament envelope, neuromuscular control, frailty and functional reserve. Perioperatively, automated frailty and sarcopenia phenotyping, wearable gait analysis and multimodal temporal models integrating imaging, electronic health records, laboratory data, medications, patient-reported outcomes and wearable signals may support dynamic risk prediction. After discharge, continuous monitoring of mobility, sleep, pain trajectories, wound-related symptoms and rehabilitation adherence may help close the high-risk surveillance gap during the 90-day postoperative episode. However, clinical adoption requires more than high discrimination. Explainable AI should be understood as one component of a broader trust framework that also includes calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision-curve analysis, external and prospective validation, workflow integration, post-deployment monitoring and accountability. The future of orthopaedic AI is not simply better diagnosis or more precise surgery, but longitudinal, multimodal support across the full care continuum: predicting progression, selecting treatment, personalizing surgery, optimizing perioperative care, monitoring recovery and preserving mobility and independence. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level IV.

title: Outcomes of Osseous Microvascular Midface Reconstruction: Does Union Matter?
abstract: Objective(s) To assess rates of bony union and their correlation with postoperative complications following osseous orbitomaxillary microvascular reconstruction. Methods A retrospective review was performed of patients who underwent orbitozygomaticomaxillary reconstruction with composite osseous free flaps at an academic medical center from 2011 to 2024. Demographics, intraoperative variables, and postoperative outcomes were collected. Univariable and multivariable regression analyses were conducted to evaluate factors associated with bony union. Results Fifty-nine patients were identified, with a mean follow-up of 3.53 years. Most subjects underwent maxillary reconstruction following oncologic resection (72.9%). The predominant flap used was the fibula free flap (78.0%), followed by the osteocutaneous radial forearm flap (16.9%). Complication rates included hardware extrusion (25.4%), fistula formation (40.7%), and bone exposure (15.3%). The rate of complete bony union was 50.0%, with partial and nonunion rates of 13.3% and 37.7%, respectively. Nonunion was more likely among patients with fistula formation (OR 4.29, p = 0.038) and those who underwent subsequent free flap (OR 8.46, p = 0.008). Multivariable regression found nonunion was associated with increasing number of sites of possible osteosynthesis (OR 36.8, p = 0.007), use of Virtual Surgical Planning (VSP) (OR 100.5, p = 0.045), and postoperative radiation therapy (OR 13.8, p = 0.032). Age, ASA class, surgeon, flap type, use of locking versus non-locking plates, ischemia time, and time from surgery to CT were not associated with nonunion. Conclusion Nonunion occurred in approximately one third of cases and was associated with increasing sites of possible osteosynthesis, use of VSP, adjuvant radiation, fistula formation, and subsequent free flap. Level of evidence: 4

title: Confocal Ex Vivo Margin Assessment in Transoral Laser Cordectomy: A Pilot Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
abstract: Objectives Margin assessment in transoral laser microsurgery (TLM) for glottic squamous cell carcinoma is challenging due to specimen size, fragmentation, and artifacts. This study evaluated the feasibility and preliminary diagnostic performance of the Histolog Scanner, an ultra-fast ex vivo confocal microscopy system, for intraoperative margin assessment in TLM cordectomy. Methods This prospective pilot study evaluated adult patients undergoing TLM cordectomy for glottic squamous cell carcinoma. Five predefined margins per specimen (anterior, posterior, superior, inferior, deep) were evaluated using Histolog Scanner and compared with conventional hematoxylin and eosin histopathology, used as the reference standard. Concordance, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and diagnostic accuracy were assessed. Results Nineteen patients were included, yielding to 95 evaluable margins. Overall concordance between Histolog Scanner and histopathology was 92.6% (88/95 margins). The scanner identified 12 true-positive, 76 true-negative, five false-positive, and two false-negative margins. Sensitivity was 85.7% (95% CI: 57.2-98.2), specificity 93.8% (95% CI: 86.2-98.0), positive predictive value 70.6% (95% CI: 44.0-89.7), negative predictive value 97.4% (95% CI: 91.0-99.7), and accuracy 92.6% (95% CI: 85.4-97.0). Agreement was substantial (Cohen's kappa = 0.73). Mean acquisition time was 13 min per specimen. Conclusion The Histolog Scanner is a feasible, rapid intraoperative screening tool with high specificity and excellent negative predictive value for ruling out involved margins in TLM cordectomy. It serves as an intraoperative adjunct rather than a replacement for definitive histopathology, which remains essential. Larger multicenter studies are required before widespread clinical setting implementation. Level of evidence: 3

The Histolog Scanner is a feasible, rapid intraoperative screening tool with high specificity and excellent negative predictive value for ruling out involved margins in TLM cordectomy. It serves as an intraoperative adjunct rather than a replacement for definitive histopathology, which remains essential. Larger multicenter studies are required before widespread clinical setting implementation.

title: Intraoperative Bone Marrow Frozen Sections Reduce Positive Final Margins in Mandibulectomy.
abstract: Objectives To assess the impact of intraoperative bone marrow frozen section (IBMFS) use on final margin status and survival outcomes in patients undergoing mandibulectomy for squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and non-SCC neoplasms. Methods A single-center retrospective cohort study was performed of patients undergoing segmental or marginal mandibulectomy for benign or malignant neoplasms between 2009 and 2025. The medical record was reviewed for demographic data, histopathologic disease features, treatment, and outcomes. Univariable and multivariable Cox regression analyses were used to evaluate associations between IBMFS and recurrence-free and overall survival among patients with SCC. Results Of 235 cases, IBMFS were performed in 80.4%. IBMFS analysis was associated with reduced rates of positive final bone margins (1.1% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.014) and overall positive margins (7.9% vs. 19.6%, p = 0.029). Positive IBMFS rate was higher among non-SCC neoplasms than SCC (23.5% vs. 3.5%, p = 0.007), with no significant difference in rate of final positive margins. IBMFS results demonstrated 90.0% sensitivity, 99.4% specificity, and 98.9% concordance with final histopathology. Among SCC patients, IBMFS use was not significantly associated with recurrence-free survival (aHR 0.671, p = 0.320) or overall survival (aHR 0.967, p = 0.923); only nodal disease and age were significantly associated with survival. Conclusions In this retrospective single-center cohort, IBMFS use was associated with improved final margin control across tumor types, including non-SCC neoplasms. Although no survival benefit was demonstrated, its association with margin clearance suggests that IBMFS may be a useful intraoperative adjunct in mandibulectomy for head and neck neoplasms. Level of evidence: 3

title: Early Oral Gastrografin Followed by Immediate CT for Precise Leak Localization and Surgical Planning After Total Laryngectomy.
abstract: Purpose Pharyngocutaneous fistula (PCF) is the most common and clinically significant complication following total laryngectomy, often leading to delayed recovery and increased morbidity. Accurate and early detection of pharyngeal leak is critical; however, conventional imaging modalities such as contrast swallow studies and computed tomography (CT) have limitations in precise anatomical localization. Materials and methods This retrospective cohort study included 117 patients who underwent total laryngectomy between January 2020 and December 2025. Patients were divided into two groups according to the postoperative imaging protocol: Gastrografin swallow followed by immediate CT (Gastrografin-CT group, n = 22) and conventional imaging ( n = 95). Leak localization was assessed using a four-point ordinal scale, and surgically actionable localization was defined as a score ≥ 2. Clinical outcomes and impact on management were also evaluated. Results The Gastrografin-CT protocol demonstrated significantly improved leak localization compared with conventional imaging (mean localization score: 3.00 ± 0.00 vs. 1.62 ± 0.83, p = 0.01). Surgically actionable localization was achieved in all patients in the Gastrografin-CT group compared with 51.2% in the conventional group ( p = 0.03). Leaks were identified on initial imaging in 100% of patients in the Gastrografin-CT group versus 82.9% in the conventional group. Although clinical outcomes, including time to oral feeding, complication rates, and hospital stay, did not significantly differ, the Gastrografin-CT protocol provided more precise anatomical delineation, facilitating targeted surgical planning. Conclusion Performing CT immediately after an oral Gastrografin swallow significantly improves anatomical localization of pharyngeal leaks following total laryngectomy. By integrating leak detection and anatomical delineation in a single imaging session, this protocol enhances surgical decision-making and may serve as a practical adjunct for postoperative evaluation and management of PCF.
