title: Atypical Stafne bone defect: a systematic review.
abstract: Objectives Atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs) may be challenging to identify because they deviate from the typical posterior mandibular presentation. This systematic review aims to analyze and synthesize the radiographic, anatomical, and histological characteristics of atypically located SBDs reported in the literature and to assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. Materials and methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted in the PubMed, Scopus, Embase, and Web of Science databases up to January 2026. Eligibility criteria included English-language case reports and case series describing atypically located Stafne bone defects (SBDs). Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were performed independently by two reviewers using an adapted assessment tool for case reports. Results Seventy studies encompassing 91 atypical cases were included. Atypically located SBDs were most frequently reported in the anterior mandible. Despite their variable localization, these defects share key anatomical and radiographic features with classical SBDs, including well-defined unilocular radiolucencies and lingual cortical depressions. Advanced imaging modalities, particularly cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), play an important role in confirming these features and in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. Histological analysis, when available, most commonly revealed normal salivary gland tissue without evidence of neoplastic transformation. Conclusions Atypically located SBDs demonstrate consistent radiographic and anatomical characteristics that may assist clinicians in orienting the diagnostic hypothesis. This review improves the understanding of this under-recognized anatomical variant and highlights the importance of appropriate imaging evaluation in ambiguous cases. Clinical relevance Recognition of these features may facilitate accurate diagnosis and help avoid unnecessary invasive procedures.

title: Validation of 3D intraoral scanner use for detecting caries lesions around dental restorations: A diagnostic accuracy study.
abstract: Objectives This study aimed to validate the use of a 3D intraoral scanner (IOS) for detecting secondary caries lesions around restorations using image-based CARS-derived severity categories, compared with visual-tactile clinical examination. Materials and methods A diagnostic validation study was conducted at the university clinical facilities, from July 2023 to September 2024, including adult patients with amalgam or composite resin restorations on anterior and posterior teeth. The restorations were assessed using visual-tactile clinical examination, adopted as the clinical reference standard, and IOS image-based assessment. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, binary-classification AUC, and clinical-IOS agreement were estimated. Confidence intervals for diagnostic accuracy measures were obtained using participant-level cluster bootstrap resampling. Results A total of 299 restorations in 41 patients were assessed. IOS sensitivity varied, with 75% (95% CI: 66.2-82.0) at the initial lesion threshold, 40% (95% CI: 20.8-57.7) at the moderate lesion threshold, and 57.1% (95% CI: 33.3-100.0) at the severe lesion threshold. Specificity was consistently high, with 84.1% (95% CI: 78.7-89.4), 97.4% (95% CI: 95.6-99.2), and 99.7% (95% CI: 98.7-99.7) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Binary-classification AUC values were 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75-0.84), 0.69 (95% CI: 0.58-0.78), and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.66-1.00) at the initial, moderate, and severe lesion thresholds, respectively. Positive predictive value was highest at the severe lesion threshold (80%), while the negative predictive value was especially high at this threshold (99%). Exact clinical-IOS agreement was 77.9%, whereas linearly weighted observed agreement was 91.1%, with a linearly weighted kappa coefficient of 0.53. Conclusions The 3D intraoral scanner is a complementary tool for assessing secondary caries lesions, showing high specificity across lesion thresholds. Sensitivity varied according to lesion severity and was less precise at the severe threshold due to the small number of severe lesions. Future research should increase sample sizes and explore combining IOS with other diagnostic methods to improve detection, especially for moderate lesions and higher caries prevalence. Clinical relevance Conventional IOS images may assist in documenting and assessing visible changes around restorations. Clinical interpretation should consider the observed sensitivity limitations and incorporate visual-tactile examination and radiographic assessment when indicated.

title: Selective preoperative lower extremity computed tomography angiography before mandibular reconstruction: Identifying patients unlikely to require fibula free flap reconstruction.
abstract: Purpose Not every patient undergoing mandibular continuity resection requires free fibula flap (FFF) reconstruction. Whether clinical judgment reliably identifies patients unlikely to benefit from preoperative lower-extremity computed tomography angiography (CTA) remains unknown, despite the relevance of this question for cost-conscious and resource-efficient imaging strategies. Methods A retrospective outcome-based validation was conducted in patients undergoing mandibular continuity resection between July 2012 and June 2023. The primary outcome was secondary FFF reconstruction among patients not initially selected for CTA. Factors associated with CTA utilization were assessed by multivariable logistic regression. Results 316 consecutively operated patients were included. Prior radiotherapy (OR 2.67, p = 0.005) and smoking history (OR 1.98, p = 0.032) were independently associated with CTA utilization. Among 111 patients without primary FFF reconstruction, four (3.6%) required secondary FFF reconstruction, all of whom had undergone CTA. No patient managed without CTA subsequently required FFF reconstruction. Conclusions In this cohort, clinical judgment was associated with successful identification of patients who did not subsequently require fibular reconstruction. Omission of CTA in carefully selected patients was not associated with subsequent reconstructive deficiency, though larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Germinoma in late adulthood with extensive dissemination: a case report and literature review.
abstract: Central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS GCTs) are exceptionally rare in patients aged 60 years or older. We report a 61-year-old man with progressive weight loss and endocrine dysfunction over 20 months, in whom magnetic resonance imaging revealed enhancing lesions including the suprasellar and sellar regions, optic tracts, ventricular walls, corpus callosum, and dorsal medulla. Biopsy findings supported a diagnosis of germinoma in the sampled tissue, and DNA methylation profiling demonstrated a molecular profile consistent with conventional germinoma. The patient underwent whole ventricular irradiation and carboplatin-etoposide chemotherapy. Febrile neutropenia during the first cycle required subsequent etoposide dose reductions, but he achieved marked radiographic regression. A descriptive review identified five cases, including the present case, for which sufficient individual clinicopathological information was available. This case highlights that CNS GCTs in older adults may radiologically mimic primary CNS lymphoma and that integrated pathological assessment, including morphology and immunohistochemistry, is essential for diagnosis. In this diagnostically challenging presentation, DNA methylation profiling provided complementary molecular support for the histopathological diagnosis of conventional germinoma.

The patient underwent whole ventricular irradiation and carboplatin-etoposide chemotherapy. Febrile neutropenia during the first cycle required subsequent etoposide dose reductions, but he achieved marked radiographic regression. A descriptive review identified five cases, including the present case, for which sufficient individual clinicopathological information was available. This case highlights that CNS GCTs in older adults may radiologically mimic primary CNS lymphoma and that integrated pathological assessment, including morphology and immunohistochemistry, is essential for diagnosis. In this diagnostically challenging presentation, DNA methylation profiling provided complementary molecular support for the histopathological diagnosis of conventional germinoma.

title: Volumetric analysis of thalamic nuclei in children with vasovagal syncope.
abstract: Aim This study aimed to investigate regional thalamic nuclei volumes in pediatric patients with vasovagal syncope (VVS) using automated MRI-based segmentation and compare these measurements with those of pediatric controls. Materials and methods This retrospective case-control study included 76 pediatric patients with VVS and 34 age- and sex-comparable controls (total n = 110) who underwent brain magnetic resonance imaging. Thalamic nuclei were segmented using the FreeSurfer automated pipeline. Group differences were assessed using multivariate and univariate analyses of covariance adjusted for age, sex, and total intracranial volume. False discovery rate correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Results Total right, left, and bilateral thalamic volumes did not differ significantly between groups (P = 0.802, P = 0.267, and P = 0.366, respectively). However, significant regional volumetric differences were identified in selected nuclei. Compared with controls, patients with VVS had larger left medial thalamic (P < 0.001), left pulvinar (P < 0.001), right pulvinar (P < 0.001), and right habenular (P < 0.001) volumes, and smaller right anterior ventral (P = 0.004), left mediodorsal (P = 0.003), and left intralaminar/midline (P = 0.012) volumes. After false discovery rate correction, corresponding q values were < 0.001, < 0.001, < 0.001, 0.002, 0.018, 0.017, and 0.043, respectively. Conclusion Children with VVS demonstrated regional volumetric differences in specific thalamic nuclei despite preserved total thalamic volume. The clinical and functional significance of these findings and their potential relationship to autonomic regulation remain uncertain. Further prospective studies incorporating functional and multimodal neuroimaging are warranted.

title: Cerebrospinal fluid positive for SARS-CoV-2 associated with neurological manifestations and proteome alterations in a multiple myeloma patient.
abstract: Background Although SARS-CoV-2 infection is primarily associated with respiratory symptoms, neurological complications have been increasingly recognized, even in the absence of pulmonary involvement. Case presentation We report a case of a 67-year-old woman with a history of multiple myeloma and recent exposure to a COVID-19-positive individual who developed rapidly progressive neurological symptoms, including dysarthria, dysphagia, and hypoesthesia, without any respiratory manifestations. Her condition deteriorated to focal and dyscognitive status epilepticus, requiring mechanical ventilation. Brain MRI showed imaging features consistent with rhombencephalitis. SARS-CoV-2 infection was confirmed through positive qRT-PCR results from both nasopharyngeal swab and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Further analysis of the CSF using quantitative shotgun proteomics via mass spectrometry revealed a neuroinflammatory profile indicative of blood-brain barrier disruption and differential expression of several proteins relevant to brain function, including the major prion protein, superoxide dismutase 1 (SOD-1), and other aggregation-prone proteins. Conclusions This case supports the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 can invade the central nervous system and cause severe neurological impairment, even in the absence of typical respiratory symptoms. The findings underscore the importance of considering SARS-CoV-2 in the differential diagnosis of rapidly progressive neurological syndromes and highlight the need for further investigation into the mechanisms of neuroinvasion and the potential neurotropism of emerging viral variants.

title: Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow: from diagnosis to rehabilitation.
abstract: Background Ulnar neuropathy at the elbow (UNE) is the second most common entrapment neuropathy of the upper limb, involving physical medicine and rehabilitation, neurology, orthopedics, and plastic surgery. It results from static or dynamic ulnar nerve instability, cubital tunnel syndrome, or space-occupying lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires thorough history, clinical examination, and selection of appropriate diagnostic tests. Search strategy PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Web of Science were searched (January 2000-August 2026) using combinations of "ulnar neuropathy", "cubital tunnel syndrome", "elbow", "ultrasound", "electrodiagnosis", "conservative treatment", "rehabilitation" and "surgery". English-language original studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses were eligible; case reports were included only where no higher-level evidence existed. Approximately 220 records were screened; 58 were retained, following SANRA recommendations for narrative reviews. Discussion High-resolution ultrasound provides dynamic, non-invasive, cost-effective evaluation of the ulnar nerve and real-time assessment of compression or instability, and guides minimally invasive procedures such as perineural injections, although the only randomized placebo-controlled trial did not show superiority of corticosteroid injection over placebo. Conservative treatment is usually first-line, although surgery may be required in advanced or refractory cases; comparative evidence shows no clear superiority among surgical techniques, while endoscopic decompression carries a higher complication rate than open approaches. Conclusions This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic pathways and therapeutic options for UNE, highlighting the role of ultrasound as both a diagnostic and interventional tool, and outlines gaps in the literature regarding standardized conservative and surgical protocols.

title: First report of proven Fusarium brachygibbosum sinusitis in a paediatric patient with acute myeloblastic leukaemia.
abstract: Purpose Fusarium brachygibbosum is an environmental mould belonging to the Fusarium sambucinum species complex (FSAMSC) and is only exceptionally reported as a human pathogen. Invasive fusariosis is a recognized complication in patients with hematological malignancies; however, proven infection caused by F. brachygibbosum has not previously been described. We report the first case of proven breakthrough sinusitis in a pediatric female with refractory acute myeloblastic leukaemia (AML) receiving posaconazole prophylaxis. Methods We describe the clinical presentation, microbiological diagnosis, antifungal susceptibility profile, treatment, and outcome of a 13-year-old neutropenic female with refractory AML who developed invasive fungal sinusitis. Species identification was established by Sanger sequencing of the elongation factor 1-alpha, and antifungal susceptibility testing was performed according to the EUCAST reference method. Results Computed tomography revealed extensive paranasal sinus involvement, and direct microscopy of sinus tissue demonstrated hyaline septate hyphae. Culture yielded a mould initially misidentified by MALDI-TOF MS as F. chlamydosporium. Molecular sequencing confirmed F. brachygibbosum. The isolate exhibited elevated Minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) to amphotericin B, azoles, echinocandins, and olorofim, while fosmanogepix showed a lower in vitro MIC. Extensive surgical debridement combined with liposomal amphotericin B, voriconazole, and subsequently olorofim was performed. Despite local control of the sinonasal infection and no microbiological or histopathological evidence of dissemination, the patient died 23 days after diagnosis. The death occurred in the context of progressive refractory AML, invasive fungal disease, pulmonary abnormalities, and subsequent neutropenic complications. Conclusion This report represents the first proven pediatric case of invasive sinusitis caused by F. brachygibbosum (FSAMSC) isolate with higher MICs to classical antifungals. The case highlights the diagnostic limitations of MALDI-TOF MS for rare Fusarium species, the value of molecular identification and antifungal susceptibility testing, and the emergence of environmental moulds breakthrough fungal infections. It also underscores the urgent need for effective novel antifungal agents against resistant Fusarium species.

title: Screening strategies for the early detection of non-cardia gastric cancer in low- to moderate-prevalence regions: Asia-Pacific gastroesophageal cancer congress consensus 2026.
abstract: Background Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden, and early detection is essential for improving patient outcomes. Although GC screening has been widely implemented in East Asian countries with a high disease burden, the optimal screening strategy for low- to moderate-prevalence regions remains unclear. To address this gap, the Asia Pacific Gastroesophageal Cancer Congress (APGCC) convened an international consensus meeting to develop evidence-based recommendations for improving the detection of non-cardia gastric cancer (NCGC). Methods The APGCC working group developed 11 clinical questions (CQs) addressing GC screening, with a particular focus on NCGC. For each CQ, assigned authors conducted literature reviews using PubMed and prepared evidence summaries and draft recommendations. Consensus was achieved through a two-round modified Delphi process involving 37 international voting members. Results The consensus recommendations addressed population-based screening, screening modalities, identification of high-risk individuals, quality indicators for esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), image-enhanced endoscopy, and artificial intelligence-assisted endoscopy. Population-based endoscopic screening is not recommended in low- to moderate-prevalence regions because of insufficient evidence. However, if screening is performed, EGD is preferred over upper gastrointestinal series for the detection of early NCGC in asymptomatic individuals. The recommendations also emphasize the importance of high-quality endoscopic examinations, risk-stratified screening using serum biomarkers, and the appropriate integration of advanced endoscopic technologies. Conclusions These APGCC consensus recommendations provide practical guidance for improving the early detection of NCGC in low- to moderate-prevalence regions. This consensus also highlights important evidence gaps and establishes a framework for future research and the development of region-specific GC screening strategies.

title: A preoperative risk-scoring model for predicting intraoperative hemorrhage during endoscopic submucosal dissection for gastric neoplasms.
abstract: Background Intraoperative hemorrhage is the most frequent complication of endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD). We aim to develop and externally validate a preoperative risk-scoring model for predicting intraoperative hemorrhage during ESD for gastric neoplasms. Methods Patients who underwent ESD for gastric neoplasms from four endoscopy centers were enrolled in this retrospective study, with 1123 patients in derivation cohort and 345 patients in validation cohort. In derivation cohort, univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis were used to identify independent preoperative predictors of intraoperative hemorrhage. A risk-scoring model was created by assigning weighted points to selected predictors. External validation was conducted to analyse the discrimination and calibration of the prediction model. Results A prediction model for intraoperative hemorrhage included 5 variables: upper-third location (5 points), large lesion size (≥ 25 mm) (4 points), current HP infection (3 points), junior endoscopist (3 points) and middle-third location (2 points). Patients were stratified into low- (0-2 points), intermediate- (3-4 points), high- (5-6 points), and very high-risk (≥ 7 points) groups, with corresponding bleeding rates of 4.8%, 35.9%, 80.2% and 98.5%, respectively. In external validation cohort, the model showed excellent discrimination, with a c-statistic of 0.96 (95% CI 0.95-0.98), and good calibration (calibration-in-the-large, - 0.04; calibration slope, 0.94). Conclusions We developed a preoperative risk-scoring model to predict intraoperative hemorrhage of ESD for gastric neoplasms. For lesions of large size or located on the upper-third of the stomach, ESD should be performed by senior endoscopists after successful HP eradication to minimize the occurrence of bleeding.

title: A comprehensive analysis of the association of psychological profiling and sagittal balance parameters with neck pain in a non-deformity cervical spondylosis population: A prospective two-centers cross-sectional study.
abstract: Purpose to comprehensively identify determining factors of perceived neck pain in a non-deformity population, integrating psychological and sagittal balance parameters.Methods a cross-sectional study of prospectively collected data was conducted on patients admitted for cervical spondylosis at two tertiary university hospitals between April 2024 and August 2025. Eligible cases were retrieved from the PANDA Registry. Records were excluded if standing X-ray was unavailable and/or not-evaluable (e.g. shoulder prosthesis); or if the admission pathology involved the cranio-cervical junction, tumors, deformities, spinal cord disease, or infections. Preoperative data included demographic, clinical (VAS neck), psychological (SCL-27, I-TIPI, CD-RISC10), and sagittal balance variables (McGregor slope, C1-C2 lordosis, C2 slope, C2-C7 lordosis, cSVA, T1 slope, cervical mismatch). Correction for multiple comparisons was applied within pre-specified hypothesis domains.Results one-hundred-thirty records were included. Intra-rater reliability for radiographic parameters was excellent (> 0.9). After categorization of patients by neck pain severity, pairwise analysis showed that only C1-C2 lordosis remained significantly higher in patients exhibiting severe neck pain (VAS < 7 vs. VAS ≥ 7). When stratified for moderate-to-severe neck pain (VAS ≥ 4), several SCL-27 scales, namely dysthymic, vegetative, agoraphobic, sociophobic, and GSI scores, and C1C2 lordosis showed significant differences. Correlation analysis using VAS neck as the dependent variable demonstrated a significant positive correlation with SCL-27 dysthymic and vegetative scores. C1-C2 lordosis showed a significant inverse correlation with neck pain. In univariate analysis, only SCL-27 dysthymic, vegetative, and GSI scores emerged as significant univariate associations of VAS neck. After correction for multiple comparisons, the SCL-27 vegetative, dysthymic and GSI scores retained significance, whereas C1-C2 lordosis did not.Conclusion in a non-deformity population, sagittal balance parameters alone do not adequately explain patient-perceived neck pain. These findings support the preoperative use of psychological assessments, especially the SCL-27, as a useful tool in preoperative screening and individualised counselling.

title: Predictive factors associated with interval changes in STN-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative CT.
abstract: Background Brain shift during deep brain stimulation (DBS) surgery may contribute to changes in lead position. Although intracranial air volume is considered an important factor, other intraoperative factors may also influence lead displacement. This study evaluated interval changes in subthalamic nucleus (STN)-DBS lead-tip position between immediate and delayed postoperative computed tomography (CT) and investigated factors associated with these changes, including intracranial air volume and intraoperative head position. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 42 DBS leads implanted bilaterally in the STN of 21 patients with Parkinson's disease. Lead-tip coordinates were assessed using Elements software (Brainlab) on CT obtained immediately after implantation and after resolution of intracranial air. Interval displacement was defined as the difference in lead-tip coordinates between the delayed and immediate postoperative CT scans. Intraoperative head position was quantified as "Angle A," measured from the horizontal reference line to the anterior commissure-posterior commissure line. Associations between potential explanatory factors and lead-tip displacement were assessed using linear mixed-effects models with patient included as a random intercept to account for within-patient correlation between bilateral leads. Results Lead-tip positions showed significant interval displacement in the lateral, anterior, and caudal directions. In univariable mixed-effects analysis, intracranial air volume was significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.033, 95% CI 0.018-0.048, p < 0.001), whereas Angle A was not (β = -0.030, 95% CI - 0.067-0.007, p = 0.111). In a multivariable mixed-effects model including intracranial air volume and Angle A, intracranial air volume remained significantly associated with anterior displacement (β = 0.0289, 95% CI 0.0110-0.0469, p = 0.002), while a larger Angle A was associated with less anterior displacement (β = -0.0270, 95% CI - 0.0535 to - 0.0004, p = 0.047). Conclusions Intracranial air volume was consistently associated with anterior STN-DBS lead-tip displacement between immediate and delayed postoperative CT. Intraoperative head position was also associated with anterior displacement after adjustment for intracranial air volume, although this finding was of borderline statistical significance and should be considered exploratory. These findings support efforts to minimize intracranial air entry during DBS implantation, while the potential influence of intraoperative head positioning requires further prospective investigation.

title: Multimodal MRI fusion and three-dimensional reconstruction for preoperative assessment of neurovascular compression in trigeminal neuralgia: A retrospective study.
abstract: Background Microvascular decompression is the primary surgical intervention for trigeminal neuralgia aimed at resolving neurovascular compression. Given the potential surgical risks, accurate preoperative assessment of neurovascular compression is critical. Although 3D visualization has been applied to preoperative assessment of neurovascular relationships, quantitative evaluation of the trigeminal nerve-vessel relationship and its association with intraoperative NVC findings remains limited. Materials and methods We retrospectively analyzed data from trigeminal neuralgia patients, hemifacial spasm controls and healthy controls. Preoperative 3D-FIESTA and 3D-TOF-MRA data were acquired and processed for 3D fusion reconstruction using 3D Slicer. After validating the model's reliability against intraoperative findings, trigeminal nerves were stratified into four subgroups. Anatomical morphological parameters and neurovascular relationships were quantitatively measured and compared among the subgroups. Immediate postoperative outcomes in trigeminal neuralgia patients were also evaluated. Results A total of 92 trigeminal neuralgia patients, 99 hemifacial spasm controls and 30 healthy controls were enrolled. The trigeminal neuralgia cohort was significantly older than the control group (63.1 vs. 54.3 years, P < 0.05). The preoperative 3D reconstruction demonstrated high consistency with intraoperative findings (accuracy: 93%, Kappa: 0.89). ROC analysis identified an optimal neurovascular distance threshold of 1.23 mm for predicting intraoperative neurovascular compression (AUC = 0.957). Morphological analysis showed no significant intergroup difference in nerve diameter (P = 0.458), whereas cisternal length differed significantly among the five groups (P < 0.001). The TNS group showed the shortest mean neurovascular distance (1.1 mm, P < 0.001) and the highest prevalence of neurovascular compression (NVC) (79.3%, P < 0.001). These findings remained consistent after inclusion of healthy controls. Immediate postoperative outcomes were not significantly associated with intraoperative NVC status or the 1.23-mm neurovascular distance. Conclusion This study confirmed the high diagnostic accuracy of preoperative 3D MRI fusion. Crucially, a neurovascular distance threshold of 1.23 mm was identified as an exploratory imaging marker for definite intraoperative compression. However, this threshold should not be regarded as an independent criterion for treatment selection.

title: Performance Analysis of Laplacian Re-Decomposition-Based PET-MRI Fusion for Quantitative Imaging Biomarkers in Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
abstract: Background Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) represent critical stages along the continuum of cognitive decline. This study investigates the Laplacian Re-decomposition (LRD) method for fusing positron emission tomography (PET) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to develop a quantitative imaging biomarker for the classification of AD. Material and method Data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database were used in this study. T 1 , T 2 , T 2 -FLAIR, and T 2 *-weighted MRI sequences, together with [ 18 F]FDG-PET images, were preprocessed and fused using the LRD algorithm. Hippocampal and frontal lobe WM segmentation, performed via U-Net, enabled relative signal contrast (RSC) calculation as a quantitative biomarker for each modality and fused image. Fusion and segmentation performance were assessed using standard metrics. RSC statistically compared between diagnostic groups after adjustment for demographic confounds, and evaluated for classification performance using ROC/AUC analysis. Results The mean Dice coefficient achieved by the trained U-Net for hippocampus and frontal lobe WM segmentation were 0.93 and 0.95, respectively. ROC analysis revealed that the RSC extracted from T 1 -weighted images fused with PET outperformed other modalities for AD vs. Cognitively normal (CN) classification (AUC = 0.88, accuracy = 0.90). Also, T 2 -weighted images fused with PET, using RSC as a quantitative biomarker, achieved the best classification performance for AD vs. MCI (AUC = 0.81, accuracy = 0.81) and MCI vs. CN (AUC = 0.84, accuracy = 0.88) classification. Conclusion Our findings indicate that RSC extracted from LRD-fused images achieves competitive classification performance, supporting its potential as a quantitative biomarker for AD.

title: Diagnosis of Suspected Pituitary Microadenomas: The Complementary Role of Habitat-based Non-enhanced MRI Radiomics Features.
abstract: To develop and validate a combined model for detecting pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases using non-contrast T1-weighted sagittal (T1SAG) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and to assess its performance as a non-contrast imaging-based tool for clinical decision support.This retrospective two-center study enrolled 519 patients with suspected pituitary microadenomas, divided into a training set (n = 321), an internal validation set (n = 80), and an external test set (n = 118). Radiomics features were extracted from both the entire pituitary gland and its habitat subregions, generated via unsupervised K-means clustering. Eight predictive models were constructed using logistic regression: a clinical model, an intra-pituitary radiomics model, three individual habitat models (Habitat 1, 2, and 3), an early-fusion model combining all habitats, an ensemble model integrating the probability outputs of the three habitat models, and a combined model that integrated clinical, intra-pituitary, and the optimal fusion model. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves (ROC), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.Among all models, the combined model demonstrated the best predictive performance across all three cohorts, achieving areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.850-0.920) in the training set, 0.788 (95% CI: 0.690-0.885) in the internal validation set, and 0.796 (95% CI: 0.712-0.880) in the external test set. The combined model also achieved the highest accuracy and sensitivity across all datasets.The combined prediction model showed robust performance in distinguishing pituitary microadenomas in suspected cases, offering enhanced clinical decision support while reducing dependence on contrast-enhanced MRI examinations.

title: TriKey AutoRefine: A Stability-Aware Framework Built on Pan-organ Segmentation Radiomics for Chronic Kidney Disease Staging.
abstract: Accurate and generalizable imaging‑based staging of chronic kidney disease remains challenging due to segmentation variability, feature instability, and heterogeneous clinical presentations. To address these gaps, a clinically aligned pan‑organ radiomics workflow for multi‑class chronic kidney disease staging was proposed. A total of 587 subjects from 3 centers were included, with chest and abdominal computed tomography scans paired with clinical and body-composition measurements. Segmentation‑induced variability was quantified within the pan‑organ segmentation system, revealing systematic anatomical and feature‑level patterns that enabled the construction of a robust and generalizable feature foundation. Building on these observations, the TriKey autorefine framework was introduced as a structured refinement strategy incorporating Shapley additive explanations guided refinement, clinically informed class weighting, and automatic parameter optimization. Using this framework, strong performance was achieved across chronic kidney disease staging tasks. In the standard 5‑class setting, high discriminative ability was obtained: training macro area under the curve 0.925 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.923-0.927); validation macro area under the curve 0.875 ± 0.0087 (95% CI 0.858-0.892). In the clinically actionable 4‑class grouping, even stronger performance was observed, with a mean macro area under the curve of 0.915 ± 0.0060 (95% CI 0.903-0.927). Interpretability was further supported through radiomics-clinical correlation analyses, which confirmed that the selected pan organ features correspond to measurable physiological variations associated with chronic kidney disease progression. This study demonstrates a robust, interpretable, and clinically grounded pan‑organ radiomics pipeline for chronic kidney disease staging, providing a generalizable foundation for future pan-organ radiomics research in nephrology and broader clinical imaging applications.

title: Locate Then Classify: A Heterogeneous Dual-Teacher Consensus Framework for Semi-Supervised Mammogram Diagnosis.
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a pathway to reduce the high cost of pixel-wise annotation in mammography, but classical teacher-student methods suffer from confirmation bias under extreme label scarcity. To address this, we propose a heterogeneous dual-teacher consensus framework (DTSL). Two complementary teachers, one detail-oriented (shallow SE attention) and one semantic-oriented (deep gated modulation), retain pseudo-labels only when they agree, thereby filtering unreliable predictions. Using only 30% of pixel-level labels, DTSL recovers 81.5% of fully supervised segmentation performance (Dice Similarity Coefficient, DSC = 0.626) and achieves a calcification intersection over union (IoU) of 0.700, reducing annotation cost by 70%. It outperforms standard Mean Teacher (78.1%) and nnU-Net plus Mean Teacher (79.8%). The trained segmentation encoder is then transferred to a classification head, injecting morphological priors into malignancy diagnosis. On the INbreast dataset, our classifier attains an AUC of 0.872 and a sensitivity of 0.837, surpassing the average sensitivity of four senior radiologists (0.803) by 3.4 percentage points (p < 0.05). Our model's superior sensitivity suggests its potential as a decision-support tool to reduce false negatives in screening, warranting prospective clinical validation. Grad-CAM visualizations confirm that attention maps align with radiologists' diagnostic cues. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/BrXNetCls-0C14/ .

title: Portable Deep Learning-Assisted Device for Automated Interincisal Opening Assessment and Oral Submucous Fibrosis Lesion Identification: A Translational Clinical Study.
abstract: Oral submucous fibrosis (OSMF) is a chronic, progressive, potentially malignant disorder prevalent in Southeast Asia and the Indian subcontinent. Progressive fibrosis restricts mouth opening, making interincisal opening as a key parameter of disease staging. This study developed a portable AI-based device for automated interincisal opening measurement and OSMF lesion detection important for real-time screening and staging. A portable device powered by a quad-core ARM Cortex-A72 processor integrates a YDLiDAR depth camera for interincisal opening measurement and an intraoral camera for image acquisition. Structured inquiry into temporomandibular joint symptoms and OSMF-associated habit history reduces false-positive classification. The AI pipeline comprises buccal mucosa segmentation, OSMF classification, Stages I-III grading based on interincisal opening, and lesion detection. Model robustness is evaluated using stratified fivefold cross-validation and Grad-CAM analysis. Bland-Altman analysis assesses agreement between LiDAR and vernier-caliper measurements, while quadratic weighted Cohen's kappa evaluates agreement between AI- and clinician-assigned OSMF stages. A total of 350 OSMF (including 10 biopsy-confirmed cases) and 334 non-OSMF images were collected. U-Net with EfficientNet-B2 achieved accurate mucosal segmentation, DenseNet-121 showed the best classification performance (accuracy/F1, 0.991), and U-Net with ResNet-34 enabled lesion localization. Clinical validation in 100 subjects achieved 98.0% sensitivity, 96.0% specificity, and 97.0% accuracy. Bland-Altman analysis confirmed agreement between interincisal and vernier-caliper measurements (SD, 0.68 mm), while AI-based staging showed substantial agreement (weighted kappa k = 0.982, 95% CI 0.956-1.00). The proposed system provides a reliable, cost-effective solution for early OSMF screening and decision support in government healthcare and community settings.

title: BLIX-Ray: Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Vision-Language Models and Reinforcement Learning.
abstract: The radiology report is essential for directing the course of treatment for a patient. However, writing radiology reports is a huge burden for radiologists. Manual reporting faces challenges due to intra-labeler and inter-labeler variability, causing inconsistent patient treatment and diagnostic results, and complicating matters due to alertness and changing judgment. To address these challenges, we propose an automated radiology report generation model tailored for chest X-ray imaging. We introduce BLIX-Ray, a vision-language model (VLM) designed to generate radiology reports using a transfer learning approach. BLIX-Ray fine-tunes the pre-trained BLIP model to extract and align rich visual and textual representations suited to the medical imaging domain. We use reinforcement learning (RL) to directly optimize report generation based on language evaluation metrics in order to further enhance performance. We evaluate BLIX-Ray on two publicly available datasets: IU-Xray and CheXpert Plus. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves the highest CIDEr and BERTScore on both datasets, while n-gram-oriented baselines retain an advantage on BLEU. BLIX-Ray integrates reinforcement learning and transfer learning to improve medical report generation under limited and heterogeneous data conditions. The results highlight the potential of vision-language models to support automated and standardized radiology reporting. Notably, BLIX-Ray achieves the best reported CIDEr (0.6534) and BERTScore (0.8765) among the compared methods on IU-Xray and leads on CIDEr, METEOR, and BERTScore on CheXpert Plus (BERTScore 0.8407), demonstrating strong report-level consensus and semantic similarity with the reference reports.

title: Foundation Models and Multimodal Learning for Medical Data with Applications in Oncology.
abstract: The rapid expansion of medical data, including radiological imaging, digital pathology, molecular profiling, electronic health records, and longitudinal clinical narratives, has created new opportunities for AI in healthcare, while also exposing the limitations of traditional unimodal modeling approaches. Multimodal learning addresses these challenges by integrating heterogeneous data sources, and recent advances in foundation models, large-scale pretrained models designed for broad task transfer, have further accelerated this shift. Together, these developments have given rise to multimodal foundation models that aim to learn generalizable, aligned representations across diverse clinical modalities. In this review, we provide an overview of multimodal foundation models in medical AI, with a particular focus on oncology. We first outline key medical data modalities and the machine learning objectives that motivate multimodal integration, including predictive, representational, and alignment-based goals. We then examine core architectural design patterns and training paradigms underlying multimodal foundation models, such as modality-specific encoders, fusion strategies, attention mechanisms, contrastive pretraining, and scalable self-supervised learning. Building on this foundation, we survey representative multimodal models across radiology, pathology, clinical text, and molecular domains. We further review applications of multimodal foundation models across the cancer care continuum, including early detection, diagnosis and subtyping, prognosis, therapy response prediction, and longitudinal survival modeling. Finally, we discuss critical challenges that limit clinical translation, including cross-institutional heterogeneity, temporal misalignment across modalities, weak supervision, interpretability, regulatory constraints, and workflow integration, and outline future directions for advancing safe and effective deployment in real-world oncology practice.

title: An Automated Machine Learning Based Framework for Scan Level Coronary Artery Calcium Risk Stratification.
abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring plays a crucial role in the early detection and risk stratification of coronary artery disease (CAD). Current techniques for CAC analysis rely on manual annotations by clinicians and large curated training datasets. This study introduces a fully automatic framework for CAC risk stratification that eliminates the need for manual clinical annotations. We introduce a novel pixel-attenuation-based feature extraction pipeline for automatic CAC assessment that leverages pseudo-labelling to identify regions of interest, reducing reliance on expert annotations. We compared our method against two alternative feature extraction strategies: a radiomics-based pipeline and a foundation-model-based pipeline. Our study focuses on non-contrast images from coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) scans. Training and testing were conducted on an in-house electrocardiogram (ECG)-gated CCTA dataset comprising 182 patients, categorized into risk groups based on CAC scores. We further investigated the impact of training exclusively on non-contrast data versus a combined dataset of contrast-enhanced and non-contrast scans, while all evaluations performed solely on non-contrast images. To assess generalizability, we applied our pipeline to the publicly available COCA-Coronary Calcium and Chest CTs dataset, demonstrating robust performance even on lower-quality, non-gated scans. The pixel-attenuation feature extraction pipeline outperformed radiomics and deep learning approaches for CAC risk classification, with accuracies of 92%, 93%, and 87%, and F1-scores of 92%, 90%, and 78% across the two-, three-, and five-class classification tasks, respectively. We present a cost-effective and time-efficient framework for early CAD patient stratification that can be implemented in clinical settings while reducing additional diagnostic procedures.

title: Diagnostic Performance and Concordance of a BI-RADS-Output AI System in Mammography: A Retrospective Study of Radiologists-AI Collaboration.
abstract: The identification of breast cancer using mammography and ultrasonography is influenced by inter-observer variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) models for breast classification have been investigated, but limited reports exist on Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS)-output AI systems. This study attempted to assess a BI-RADS-output AI system by comparing breast cancer detection rates among radiologist-only, AI-only, and combined interpretations, while also focusing on the AI's ability to identify cancers missed by radiologists and analyzing diagnostic concordance concerning imaging features and BI-RADS categories. A retrospective analysis was performed on 331 lesions from 321 consecutive breast cancer patients who underwent preoperative digital mammography and ultrasonography. McNemar's test was used to find the detection rates, and chi-square/Fisher's test, Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC) analysis, and Kappa statistics were used to verify the diagnostic performance. The combined radiologist-AI interpretation achieved the highest cancer detection rate of 90.6%, which was higher than the radiologist's rate of 87.6% and the AI's rate of 84.0% (P < 0.05). The advantage was especially evident for BI-RADS 4B lesions, where AI alone decreased to 54.4%, while the combined method increased to 81.8%. AI found tumors that radiologists missed, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.840. There was a strong agreement for microcalcifications (κ = 0.827), but only a weak to moderate agreement for mass morphology and final BI-RADS classification (κ = 0.142-0.414). Although AI-radiologist agreement varied across different imaging features, their complementary strengths enabled improved cancer detection performance, supporting the role of BI-RADS-output AI systems as clinical decision-support tools rather than replacements for radiologists.

A retrospective analysis was performed on 331 lesions from 321 consecutive breast cancer patients who underwent preoperative digital mammography and ultrasonography. McNemar's test was used to find the detection rates, and chi-square/Fisher's test, Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC) analysis, and Kappa statistics were used to verify the diagnostic performance. The combined radiologist-AI interpretation achieved the highest cancer detection rate of 90.6%, which was higher than the radiologist's rate of 87.6% and the AI's rate of 84.0% (P < 0.05). The advantage was especially evident for BI-RADS 4B lesions, where AI alone decreased to 54.4%, while the combined method increased to 81.8%. AI found tumors that radiologists missed, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.840. There was a strong agreement for microcalcifications (κ = 0.827), but only a weak to moderate agreement for mass morphology and final BI-RADS classification (κ = 0.142-0.414). Although AI-radiologist agreement varied across different imaging features, their complementary strengths enabled improved cancer detection performance, supporting the role of BI-RADS-output AI systems as clinical decision-support tools rather than replacements for radiologists.

title: HCF-Net: a Hierarchical Cascade Fusion Network Aligned with Clinical Treatment Pathways for Preoperative Molecular Subtyping of Breast Cancer on Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI.
abstract: Preoperative molecular subtyping of breast cancer is essential for treatment selection and prognosis assessment, yet most deep learning approaches formulate subtype prediction as a conventional flat multi-class task without reflecting the sequential clinical decision process. We developed HCF-Net, a hierarchical cascade fusion network that decomposes subtype prediction into three clinically aligned binary decision nodes and integrates multiphase DCE-MRI with clinicoradiologic information. The model was retrospectively developed and validated using a dual-center cohort of 373 women who underwent preoperative 3.0 T multiphase DCE-MRI. On an independent test set (n = 75), HCF-Net achieved a Macro-AUC of 0.868 (95% CI, 0.806-0.923), accuracy of 73.3%, Macro-F1 of 0.732, and Cohen's κ of 0.631. The fusion model consistently achieved the highest AUC across all three hierarchical decision nodes, reaching 0.890 for luminal versus non-luminal tumors, 0.865 for Luminal A versus Luminal B tumors, and 0.974 for HER2-enriched versus triple-negative tumors. The same ordering of classification strategies was observed with a ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone. Compared with conventional flat classification strategies, hierarchical cascade decomposition and decision-level fusion provided substantial performance gains. These findings suggest that a hierarchical fusion framework aligned with clinical decision pathways may provide an effective and interpretable approach for preoperative breast cancer molecular subtype prediction.

title: Complementary Error Profiles of Human Readers and Large Language Models in Detecting AI-Generated Chest Radiographs: A Comparative Reader Study.
abstract: Frontier large language models (LLMs) and diffusion models can generate realistic chest radiographs, raising concerns for dataset integrity when provenance metadata are absent. We compared authenticity judgments by two radiologists, two nonradiologist physicians, and three frontier LLMs (GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Claude Opus 4.8) on 160 posteroanterior radiographs: 40 real NIH ChestX-ray14 images and 120 synthetic images generated from text by three pipelines. Each evaluator judged every image once; the LLM evaluation was repeated twice 3 months later. Balanced accuracy was the primary metric, given 75% synthetic prevalence. The two best evaluators reached nearly identical balanced accuracy from opposite operating points: Gemini 3.5 Flash had the highest point estimate (77.9%; specificity 100%, sensitivity 55.8%) and RAD1 was a close second (75.8%; specificity 55.0%, sensitivity 96.7%), a paired difference of - 2.1 percentage points (95% CI, - 5.8 to 1.2). On repetition, LLM judgments were not fully reproducible and this ordering did not hold. Nonradiologists performed near chance. All four human readers detected diffusion-generated images at 82-100%, whereas the radiologists misclassified 38-45% of real images and the conservative LLMs reached perfect specificity yet detected only 32-72% of LLM-generated images. With laterality markers and borders masked, specificity was 62.5% (Gemini) and 85.0% (GPT-5.5) against 90-100% in same-day unmasked runs. Interevaluator agreement was low throughout (Fleiss' kappa among LLMs 0.213). A frequency-domain baseline reached 98.3% balanced accuracy within this dataset but 12% sensitivity on a held-out generator. Human readers and LLMs failed on different images; visual authenticity assessment alone may be insufficient for provenance verification.

title: Automatic Vertebral Body Segmentation Performance in Lateral Thoracic Spine X-Rays: A Comparative Analysis Based on Implant Presence and Subtype.
abstract: Accurate vertebral body segmentation in spine radiographs is essential for quantitative analysis, but metallic implants introduce artifacts that degrade model performance. We evaluated the effects of implant presence and material subtypes on automatic segmentation using real-world thoracic spine lateral X-rays. SOLOv2 and Mask R-CNN were evaluated on radiographs from 264 patients. To analyze the localized impact of surgical hardware, a synchronized cohort of 3637 vertebral bodies correctly delineated by both models was analyzed, comparing non-implanted (n = 3467) and implanted (n = 170) instances. The implanted group was stratified into four subtypes: Bone Cement, Screw, Screw + Cement, and Screw + Etc. Performance was quantified via precision, sensitivity, Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), Hausdorff distance (HD95), and average symmetric surface distance (ASSD), and validated using the Mann-Whitney U test (α = 0.010). Implant presence caused significant performance degradation across all metrics (p < 0.001). The Screw + Etc subgroup showed the most profound degradation versus baseline (DSC: 0.826 vs. 0.930, p < 0.001). The Screw subgroup exhibited significant declines in volumetric overlap and boundary distances (p < 0.010). The Bone Cement subgroup showed a broad multidimensional decline, including a severe drop in sensitivity (p < 0.001), while the Screw + Cement subgroup demonstrated significant distance-based errors (p = 0.005). Implant presence significantly reduces thoracic spine segmentation performance, varying distinctly by subtype. Developers must account for these subtype-specific artifacts to ensure clinical validity.

title: Feasibility of Deep Learning Segmentation in Anterior Quadratus Lumborum Ultrasound Imaging: Challenges in Identifying the Injection Plane.
abstract: Accurate identification of sonoanatomy is essential for successful anterior quadratus lumborum (QL) block performance. Prior work has addressed anatomically distinct muscular and osseous structures, whereas automated segmentation of the anterior QL block injection plane has not been described. In this single-center prospective imaging study, 82 simulated anterior QL block ultrasound recordings from 42 healthy volunteers yielded 460 annotated frames across six classes, including the anterior QL block injection plane. A 2D nnU-Net model was trained using fivefold cross-validation and tested on 23 unseen clinical images acquired during routine clinical practice. Performance was assessed using Dice similarity coefficients, intersection-over-union (IoU), precision, and recall, and compared with a manually tuned 2D U-Net. The mean Dice score across all classes was 0.62, compared with 0.50 for the U-Net baseline. Performance was highest for the vertebral body (0.91) and psoas major muscle (0.86), moderate for the quadratus lumborum muscle (0.69) and transverse abdominal muscle (0.52), and lower for the posterior renal fascia (0.35) and injection plane (0.38). Precision and recall distinguished two failure modes. The posterior renal fascia was frequently missed but accurate when detected (0.74 and 0.31), whereas the injection plane was localized in nearly all cases but imprecisely delineated (0.45 and 0.38). Deep learning was feasible for segmentation of major anatomical landmarks in anterior QL ultrasound images, but remained limited for the interfascial injection plane, where the difficulty lay in boundary precision rather than detection. Further development and external validation are required before clinical application.

title: Reference-Label Construction and Annotation Reporting in CT- and MRI-Based Adipose Tissue Segmentation: A Systematic Review and Evidence Map.
abstract: CT/MRI adipose tissue segmentation underpins body-composition and medical-imaging AI research, yet reference labels are often described only as "manual," "expert," or "reference" segmentations, obscuring heterogeneity in ground-truth construction. To systematically review how reference labels, annotation procedures, validation standards, and reproducibility-relevant reporting are defined in CT- and MRI-based adipose tissue segmentation studies. The review protocol was prospectively registered in OSF Registries before the formal multi-database search. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, SpringerLink/MICCAI/LNCS, and SPIE Digital Library. Of 25,774 records, 8619 remained after deduplication, and 204 studies were included. The final corpus comprised 204 studies organized into 122 Tier 1, 64 Tier 2, and 18 Tier 3 synthesis groups. CT-family imaging accounted for 106 studies and MRI-only imaging for 67. Manual, expert, or reference labels were identified in 178 studies (87.3%), while automated or model-based computational methods were used in 181 (88.7%). External or multicenter validation was reported in 37 studies (18.1%), and reader- or operator-level reproducibility assessment in 64 (31.4%). Data availability was explicitly reported or partly available in 68 studies (33.3%), code, software, or model availability in 57 (27.9%), and label, mask, contour, or annotation availability in 3 (1.5%). Mean reporting completeness was 9.44/12; 149 studies (73.0%) had high reporting completeness, and 55 (27.0%) had moderate reporting completeness. Reference labels should be treated as provenance-bearing data objects rather than self-evident ground truth. Reproducible medical-imaging AI evaluation requires explicit reporting of compartment definitions, boundary rules, annotator roles, correction/adjudication, validation, and label availability. We propose a domain-specific annotation-chain reporting checklist that complements existing medical-imaging AI guidance by operationalizing adipose-compartment definitions, anatomical boundary rules, correction workflows, reference-label provenance, and label availability. For algorithm development, transparent annotation-chain reporting is also necessary to interpret training targets, benchmark performance, label-efficient learning, and cross-dataset validation.

title: EACC: An Entropy-Based Adversarial UDA Network with Inter-domain Channel-Wise Similarity Regularization and Pixel-Wise Contrastive Learning.
abstract: Magnetic resonance images acquired from different medical centers often exhibit substantial variations in imaging protocols and scanners, resulting in severe domain shifts that degrade the performance of brain tumor segmentation models. This study develops an effective unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework for cross-center brain tumor segmentation, enabling models trained on labeled source data to generalize to unlabeled target datasets collected from different institutions. We propose an entropy-based adversarial UDA network with inter-domain channel-wise similarity regularization and pixel-wise contrastive learning (EACC). Specifically, entropy-based adversarial learning performs global domain alignment, pixel-wise contrastive learning enhances local feature discrimination, and channel-wise similarity regularization preserves structural consistency across domains. These components collaboratively reduce domain discrepancies, thereby improving cross-center generalization. Experiments were conducted on two private datasets, Brain-FZ129 and Brain-ZZ211, using BraTS2020 as the source domain. On Brain-FZ129, EACC achieved 81.82% in Dice, 6.45 mm in 95% Hausdorff Distance (HD95), 69.38% in Jaccard Index, and 2.18 mm in average surface distance, outperforming all competing UDA methods. On Brain-ZZ211, EACC also obtained the best performance, with a Dice of 85.88% and an HD95 of 6.56 mm, ranking first among all compared methods. Furthermore, on the public BraTS-2023 SSA dataset, our method achieved 86.62% in Dice and 15.84 mm in HD95, demonstrating competitive performance and confirming the generalization capability of the proposed approach. These results indicate that EACC effectively reduces domain shifts and improves the robustness of brain tumor segmentation across heterogeneous medical centers, providing practical value for real-word clinical deployment.

title: Development and External Testing of an Interpretable MRI-Based Machine Learning Model for Differentiating Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma from Cellular Leiomyoma.
abstract: This retrospective two-center diagnostic study was aimed at developing and externally testing an interpretable MRI-based machine learning model for differentiating endometrial stromal sarcoma (ESS) from cellular leiomyoma (CL). A total of 155 women with pathologically confirmed ESS or CL were assigned to a derivation cohort (n = 111) and an external testing cohort (n = 44). Clinical variables, qualitative MRI features, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) histogram parameters were evaluated. Three MRI-derived predictors-irregular tumor margin, cystic areas on T2-weighted imaging, and mean ADC-were used to train six classifiers. The final support vector machine model with a radial basis function kernel was evaluated at a fixed threshold determined in the derivation cohort using receiver operating characteristic, calibration, decision curve, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) analyses. A reader study assessed the effect of model assistance. The model achieved areas under the curve of 0.843 (95% CI, 0.760-0.917) in the derivation cohort and 0.835 (95% CI, 0.669-0.960) in the external testing cohort. Calibration and decision curve analyses indicated acceptable performance and potential clinical utility. In an exploratory model-assisted reader analysis, junior radiologist specificity increased from 46.4 to 82.1% and accuracy from 52.3 to 77.3%. This interpretable three-feature model demonstrated promising performance across cohorts and may serve as an adjunctive tool for preoperative MRI assessment, although prospective multicenter validation is warranted.

title: Generalizability of Deep Learning Architectures for Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Classification in Histopathology: A Comparative CNN-Vision Transformer Study with External Validation and Label-Quality Analysis.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is the most prevalent oral malignancy, with delayed diagnosis contributing to poor survival. Deep learning has shown promise for histopathological detection of OSCC, but reported performance is frequently based on single-source datasets, with limited external validation and variable annotation quality. Our study was to compare representative CNN and transformer architectures for histopathological OSCC classification and assess their generalizability under external domain shift. A total of 10,817 H&E-stained image patches from 114 patients were classified as OSCC or normal/control. Images were independently reviewed by two oral pathologists, with discordant cases adjudicated by a senior pathologist (Cohen's κ = 0.975). Eight ImageNet-pre-trained architectures (ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T) were fine-tuned using three random seeds. Models were trained, validated, and tested on the internally curated dataset {MIDAS} and subsequently evaluated on two independent external datasets used exclusively for external validation. Diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, statistical significance, and model interpretability were assessed. To investigate the observed reduction in external performance, cancer-labelled images from the external datasets underwent post hoc expert pathological review for potential label discordance. A total of 10,817 H&E-stained image patches from 114 patients were classified as OSCC or normal/control. Images were independently reviewed by two oral pathologists, with discordant cases adjudicated by a senior pathologist (Cohen's κ = 0.975). Eight ImageNet-pre-trained architectures (ResNet18, ResNet50, ResNet101, DenseNet121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16, and Swin-T) were fine-tuned using three random seeds. Models were evaluated on a patient-level internal test set and two independent external datasets. Diagnostic performance, computational efficiency, statistical differences, and interpretability were assessed. Cancer-labelled images from External Dataset 2 were post hoc reassessed for label discordance. ConvNeXt-Tiny demonstrated the strongest overall performance. Substantial external degradation across models highlights the effects of domain shift and label quality, emphasizing expert annotation, independent validation, reproducible benchmarking, and multi-institutional datasets for clinical translation.

title: AutoLMISeg: A Fully Automated Pipeline for 3D Lumbar Muscle Volumetry and Densitometry on CT - Technical Validation Against an Operator-Driven Workflow.
abstract: Opportunistic body composition analysis using single-slice 2D computed tomography scans is limited by anatomical variations and field-of-view constraints. Although 3D volumetry is more comprehensive, it is not widely adopted due to the time-consuming nature of manual segmentation. The objective is to technically validate AutoLMISeg (Automated Lumbar Muscle Index Segmentation), a fully automated "zero-click" deep learning pipeline for 3D L1-L5 lumbar muscle volumetry and densitometry. Sixty-nine CT scans were analyzed retrospectively. AutoLMISeg (GPU-accelerated) was compared to a human-in-the-loop reference standard (operator-driven segmentation). Accuracy was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), and volumetric agreement was evaluated using the concordance correlation coefficient (CCC) and Bland-Altman analysis. Processing times were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. AutoLMISeg showed excellent spatial agreement, with a mean DSC of 0.928 ± 0.019. Volumetric concordance was nearly perfect (CCC = 0.971), with a negligible mean bias of + 16.32 cm 3 (approximately 2%). The automated pipeline significantly reduced processing time, completing the task in an average of 31.2 ± 7.2 s, compared to an average of 111.7 ± 25.9 s for the manual reference (p < 0.001). AutoLMISeg provides highly accurate and reliable 3D muscle biomarkers in less than a minute, making large-scale opportunistic screening in routine practice possible.

title: Gradient-Based Self-supervised Multi-task Optimization for Weakly Supervised Brain Tumor Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation requires extensive voxel-wise annotations, making fully supervised training costly and time-consuming. Weak supervision alleviates this burden but often suffers from limited accuracy. To improve label efficiency, we propose DPS-SSL: Differentiable Policy Selection Self-Supervised Learning, a gradient-based, differentiable policy selection framework for weakly supervised 3D tumor segmentation within a self-supervised multi-task learning setting. Instead of relying on fixed pretext tasks, our method learns (end-to-end) which combinations of auxiliary self-supervised tasks (rotation, flip, noise injection, blurring, jigsaw, and patch masking) and their magnitudes most benefit the segmentation objective. A gradient-driven policy mechanism dynamically identifies relevant tasks and suppresses harmful ones, while adaptive loss weighting balances contributions between main and auxiliary tasks. Experiments on the BraTS2020 and BraTS2023 datasets show that our approach achieves Whole Tumor Dice scores of 90.7% and 90.3%, respectively, approaching fully supervised performance while requiring only weak annotations. These results demonstrate that task-adaptive self-supervision provides an effective and label-efficient solution for 3D brain tumor segmentation.

title: Validating Radiomic Feature Comparisons with Patient-Specific Image Surrogates.
abstract: Radiomic features may discriminate outcomes without identifying the image property responsible for that discrimination. We evaluated a patient-specific surrogate framework that tests feature responses to explicitly defined image modifications and diagnoses limitations of the surrogate procedure itself. Four public brain tumor magnetic resonance imaging collections contributed 1699 studies passing initial quality control. Core validation used smaller subsets, including 40 depth-stratified control evaluations from 38 glioma subjects, alongside a constructive counterexample and Gaussian-null diagnostics. Thirteen quantile-based morphological and topological descriptors were compared with conventional radiomics. Binary image pairs with exactly equal distance-1 co-occurrence counts differed in Euler characteristic beyond an independent ensemble's range in 16/16 replicates, versus 0/16 negative controls. This establishes a specific limitation of those co-occurrence measurements. The Gaussian spectrum estimator was parameter-sensitive: only three of five evaluated settings satisfied an operational negative-control diagnostic, which does not establish statistical calibration. Under the depth-stratified null, the median fraction of descriptors detecting planted objects was 61.5% for the topological set, versus 13.7% and 31.5% for conventional features at 24 and 64 bins. These are descriptive, configuration-dependent comparisons; dependent features, control-based selection, and incomplete spectral convergence limit inference. Secondary clinical applications did not establish biological transferability or prognostic benefit. The framework provides reproducible tests of specified feature-null combinations, while exposing the controls and assumptions needed to interpret them.

title: Interpretable Source-Aware Bone-Muscle Fusion Framework for Multicenter Prediction of Osteoporotic Vertebral Fractures.
abstract: Osteoporotic vertebral fracture (OVF) is underrecognized, and bone mineral density (BMD) alone may be insufficient for prediction. We developed the multisource fusion model for osteoporotic vertebral fracture (MSF-OVF), an interpretable source-aware framework integrating clinical-demographic variables, BMD, and lumbar MRI-derived ventral and dorsal paraspinal muscle (PM) representations. This retrospective multicenter study included 2680 participants aged > 40 years from five centers (one training, one internal validation, four external test cohorts). Deep features from four PM regions were extracted using vision foundation model-guided transfer learning and integrated with age, sex, body mass index, and BMD through source-aware latent fusion. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), calibration, and interpretability analyses. MSF-OVF achieved an AUC of 0.881 (95% CI, 0.854-0.909) in internal validation and 0.851-0.917 across four external cohorts. Compared with the clinical-demographic and BMD baseline, MSF-OVF improved AUC by 0.046-0.093 and significantly outperformed it in internal validation and most external cohorts (DeLong P ≤ 0.034). Continuous NRI was 0.268-1.034 across all validation cohorts (P ≤ 0.011). MSF-OVF also outperformed single-muscle models (AUC, 0.454-0.736; P ≤ 0.009). After training-derived logistic recalibration, the internal validation Brier score was 0.140, with a calibration-in-the-large (CITL) of - 0.168 and calibration slope of 0.926. Class activation maps mainly highlighted PM regions. Automated segmentation took several seconds and inference 57.71 ± 18.66 ms per participant. Source-aware fusion of clinical-demographic, BMD, and PM MRI information may support computer-aided multicenter OVF prediction.

title: Annotation-Efficient Individual Muscle Segmentation from Dixon MRI: A Multi-Dataset Benchmark of Pretraining and Fat-Fraction Guidance.
abstract: Measuring individual muscles and their fatty infiltration on Dixon MRI can support sarcopenia assessment, but manual annotation is time-consuming and annotated datasets are often small. This study investigated accurate individual-muscle segmentation with limited labelled data. Three datasets were used: an abdominal CT dataset of 300 subjects with adipose-tissue labels, a lower-limb Dixon MRI dataset of 25 subjects with 13 thigh and 9 calf muscles, and an independent cohort of 66 subjects for external testing. Network architecture, encoder pretraining, a Dixon-derived fat-fraction input, and a shared CT-MRI encoder were compared. A 2.5D model, subject-level cross-validation, zero-shot transfer, label-free domain adaptation, and few-shot adaptation were also evaluated. The best models reached Dice 0.947±0.017 for CT adipose tissue and 0.925±0.010 for thigh muscle; the best 2.5D model reached 0.928, while a reported 3D Attention-Res-V-Net reached 0.857 under a different protocol. Encoder pretraining helped most at the smallest budgets, with ImageNet performing best and comparably to CT-based pretraining at eight subjects. A shared CT-MRI encoder retained accuracy with 44% fewer parameters, and thigh-muscle volumes agreed closely with reference measurements (ICC (2,1)=0.998 ). On the external cohort, fine-tuning raised Dice from 0.11 zero-shot to 0.61, 0.76, and 0.88 with four, eight, and 46 labelled target subjects. The fat-fraction input improved segmentation only when very few subjects (two or four) were labelled. Encoder pretraining and efficient model sharing help when annotated MRI data are scarce. A small amount of target-domain annotation substantially improves cross-cohort transfer, and repeated subject-level validation is important for reliable evaluation.

title: Training-Volume Analysis, Computational Efficiency, and Green AI in Rotator Cuff Calcific Tendinopathy Classification-A Two-Institution Study with External Validation.
abstract: To evaluate how training data volume influences diagnostic performance, external validation, robustness to training-subset composition, and computational efficiency in a VGG19-based model for rotator cuff calcific tendinopathy (RCCT) classification on shoulder radiographs (XRs), using training data from a single development institution. This retrospective two-institution study included 5056 shoulder XRs. A Visual Geometry Group 19 (VGG19)-based pipeline was trained on four cumulative fractions of a 4268-XRs development cohort: 25% (M25), 50% (M50), 75% (M75), and 100% (M100), using stratified 5-fold cross-validation. To assess robustness to training-subset composition, three nested cumulative sampling realizations were generated for M25, M50, and M75, while M100 represented the fixed full-data reference. Models were evaluated on an internal test cohort ( n=480 ) and an external validation cohort ( n=308 ). Areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) were compared using correlated DeLong tests with Holm adjustment. M75 and M100 were additionally assessed using two one-sided tests (TOST) with a ±0.02 AUC equivalence margin. Training-volume robustness was assessed across repeated cumulative subset realizations. Grad-CAM localization was quantitatively evaluated against expert-defined lesion regions using Pointing Game, localization area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC), and Energy-Based Pointing Game (EBPG), with Score-CAM used for qualitative corroboration. In the primary sampling realization, internal AUC increased from 0.869 with M25 to 0.951 with M100. External AUC increased from 0.835 (M25) to 0.903 (M50), 0.945 (M75), and 0.953 (M100). External improvements were significant from M25 to M50 and from M50 to M75 (both Holm-adjusted P<.001 ), whereas the M75-to-M100 increment was small ( Δ AUC=0.008; P=.161 ). M75 and M100 were externally equivalent within the ±0.02 AUC margin (TOST P=.016 ). Across three independently sampled M75 subsets, external AUC remained highly stable (0.945-0.948; mean ± standard deviation, 0.946 ± 0.001), and all three M75 realizations were equivalent to M100. Compared with M100, M75 required 11.4% less training time and 15.4% less measured energy. In the primary seed-42 realization, quantitative Grad-CAM localization generally improved with increasing training volume: M100 achieved the highest Pointing Game and localization AUPRC in both cohorts, whereas EBPG peaked at M75. Increasing training volume improved model discrimination, but external gains showed marked diminishing returns beyond M75 in this VGG19-based RCCT classification task. Near-maximal external performance at M75 was reproducible across independent training-subset realizations and statistically equivalent to full-data training within the evaluated margin, supporting training-volume analysis as a strategy for balancing performance and computational resources within this study setting. In this VGG19-based RCCT classification task using training data from a single development institution, external discrimination showed marked diminishing returns beyond 75% training volume, with highly reproducible M75 performance across independent subset realizations and statistical equivalence to full-data training within a ±0.02 AUC margin.

title: Evaluating Explicit Anatomical Priors Beyond a Mature CT Detector for Six Acute Abdominal Emergencies.
abstract: To test whether anatomical priors from a general-purpose organ segmentation model (TotalSegmentator, TS), applied at inference or during training, improve an externally validated YOLOv11 detector for six acute abdominal emergencies. The frozen detector was applied to 827 external Stanford Merlin CT studies with language-model report labels; a nested 280-study radiologist-adjudicated subset was the reference standard. TS-derived slice selection (Arm A), organ-state integration (Arm B), and their combination (Arm C) were compared with the detector alone under frozen, recalibrated, and fine-tuned conditions. The detector was also retrained from scratch (identical 10-epoch budget) with image channels only, with the patient's TS organ maps as added input channels, or with another patient's maps. AUROC was primary; comparisons used a paired study-level bootstrap. The detector generalized externally (macro AUROC 0.816 cohort; 0.879 adjudicated). Slice selection was non-inferior but not beneficial: nearly all confident detections already lay within the anchored organ's axial range; organ-state fusion improved AUROC only for cholecystitis (hypothesis-generating). In single runs, training with organ maps raised internal test mAP@0.5 (0.517 versus 0.482), and the model depended on the maps, but external macro AUROC did not improve (0.822 versus 0.829; Δ -0.007, 95% CI -0.019 to +0.007) and kidney-stone AUROC fell (0.678 versus 0.768; exploratory), unlike with another patient's maps. Per-site recalibration was the most effective operating-point adjustment (macro F1 +0.021); annotation-free fine-tuning reduced discrimination. Explicit anatomy, applied after detection or during training, did not improve this detector's overall external discrimination. Per-site recalibration gave the largest operating-point gain.
